translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 273
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 273

sentences.zh: 【後唐紀二】　起閼逢涒灘，盡旃蒙作噩十月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Tang Records 2] From Jiepeng Youtan through the tenth month of Zhanmeng Zuoe; one year and a fraction in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Tang Records 2] From the year Jiepeng Youtan through the tenth month of Zhanmeng Zuoe—slightly more than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 莊宗光聖神閔孝皇帝中同光二年（

translations.literal: Middle reign of Emperor Zhuangzong Guangchengshenminxiao, second year of Tongguang (
translations.idiomatic: Middle reign of Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang, second year of Tongguang (

sentences.zh: 甲申，公元九二四年）

translations.literal: jiashen, corresponding to the year 924 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: jiashen, AD 924)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲辰，幽州奏契丹入寇，至瓦橋。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jiachen day, Youzhou reported that the Khitan had invaded and reached Wa Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the jiachen day, Youzhou reported that Khitan forces had invaded and advanced as far as Wa Bridge.

sentences.zh: 以天平軍節度使李嗣源為北面行營都招討使，陝州留後霍彥威副之，宣徽使李紹宏為監軍，將兵救幽州。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan, military governor of Tianping, was appointed overall commander of the northern field headquarters; Huo Yanwei, acting prefect of Shanzhou, was made his deputy; and Li Shaohong, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made army supervisor, and they led troops to relieve Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan, military governor of Tianping, was appointed overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters, with Huo Yanwei, acting prefect of Shanzhou, as his deputy and Li Shaohong, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, as army supervisor; they marched to relieve Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 孔謙復言於郭崇韜曰：「首座相公萬機事繁，居第且遠，租庸簿書多留滯，宜更圖之。」

translations.literal: Kong Qian again said to Guo Chongtao, "The chief minister is overwhelmed with state affairs, his residence is distant, and the tax and corvée ledgers are often delayed; this should be reconsidered."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian again told Guo Chongtao, "The chief minister is buried in state business, lives far away, and tax and corvée paperwork keeps piling up—we ought to find another arrangement."

sentences.zh: 豆盧革嘗以手書假省庫錢數十萬，謙以手書示崇韜，崇韜微以諷革。

translations.literal: Doulu Ge had once borrowed several hundred thousand in cash from the provincial treasury on his personal note; Qian showed the note to Chongtao, and Chongtao subtly used it to admonish Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Ge had once borrowed several hundred thousand strings from the provincial treasury on his personal note; Qian showed the note to Chongtao, who used it to drop a pointed hint to Ge.

sentences.zh: 革懼，奏請崇韜專判租庸，崇韜固辭。

translations.literal: Ge, in fear, memorialized that Chongtao alone should oversee tax and corvée affairs; Chongtao firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Ge memorialized that Chongtao alone should run tax and corvée affairs, but Chongtao firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然則誰可者？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Then who is suitable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Then who is fit for the post?"

sentences.zh: 崇韜曰：「孔謙雖久典金谷，若遽委大任，恐不葉物望，請復用張憲。」

translations.literal: Chongtao said, "Although Kong Qian has long managed finances, if such a great charge were suddenly entrusted to him, I fear it would not satisfy public expectation; I ask that Zhang Xian be reappointed."
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao replied, "Kong Qian has handled finances for years, but if we suddenly give him the full portfolio, I doubt it will satisfy expectations—please bring back Zhang Xian."

sentences.zh: 帝即命召之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered him summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered Zhang Xian summoned.

sentences.zh: 謙彌失望。

translations.literal: Qian was all the more disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was bitterly disappointed.

sentences.zh: 岐王聞帝入洛，內不自安，遣其子行軍司馬彰義節度使兼侍中繼曮入貢，始上表稱臣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, hearing that the emperor had entered Luoyang, was inwardly ill at ease; he sent his son Li Jiyan, chief of staff, military governor of Zhangyi, and also chief minister, to present tribute, and for the first time submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qi learned that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he grew uneasy and sent his son Li Jiyan—chief of staff, military governor of Zhangyi, and chief minister—to present tribute and, for the first time, to submit a memorial acknowledging himself as a subject.

sentences.zh: 帝以其前朝耆舊，與太祖比肩，特加優禮，每賜詔但稱岐王而不名。

translations.literal: Because he was an elder of the former dynasty and had stood shoulder to shoulder with the founding emperor, the emperor treated him with special favor; in every edict he was addressed only as Prince of Qi, never by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: As an elder of the former court who had ranked beside the founding emperor, he received exceptional courtesy: every imperial edict addressed him only as Prince of Qi, never by his personal name.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，加繼曮兼中書令，遣還。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day, Jiyan was additionally appointed chief minister and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, Jiyan was also made chief minister and sent home.

sentences.zh: 敕：「內官不應居外，應前朝內官及諸道監軍並私家先所畜者，不以貴賤，並遣詣闕。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Inner officials should not remain outside the palace. All inner officials of the former dynasty, military supervisors of the various circuits, and those previously kept in private households, regardless of rank, are to be sent to court."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Eunuchs must not serve outside the palace. Every eunuch from the former dynasty, every circuit military supervisor, and every one kept in private households—whatever their rank—must be sent to court."

sentences.zh: 時在上左右者已五百人，至是殆及千人，皆給贍優厚，委之事任，以為腹心。

translations.literal: At that time there were already five hundred at the emperor's side; by this point the number approached a thousand. All were given generous maintenance, entrusted with duties, and regarded as his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred eunuchs already attended the emperor; after this summons the number neared a thousand. They received lavish stipends, were given real responsibilities, and were treated as his trusted inner circle.

sentences.zh: 內諸司使，自天祐以來以士人代之，至是復用宦者，浸干政事。

translations.literal: The commissioners of the inner bureaus, since the Tianyou era, had been replaced by literati; now eunuchs were again employed and gradually interfered in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tianyou era literati had held the inner bureau commissions; now eunuchs were restored and steadily encroached on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 既而復置諸道監軍，節度使出征或留闕下，軍府之政皆監軍決之，陵忽主帥，怙勢爭權，由是籓鎮皆憤怒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward military supervisors were again installed in every circuit. When a military governor campaigned or remained at court, all army headquarters affairs were decided by the supervisor, who looked down on the commander and relied on power to vie for authority; because of this the regional commands were all enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon circuit military supervisors were reinstated. Whether a military governor was in the field or detained at court, the supervisor ran army headquarters, slighted the commander, and used his position to grab power—enraging every regional command.

sentences.zh: 契丹出塞。

translations.literal: The Khitan withdrew beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan withdrew beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 召李嗣源旋師，命泰寧節度使李紹欽、澤州刺史董璋戍瓦橋。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan was recalled and his army withdrawn; Li Shaoqin, military governor of Taining, and Dong Zhang, prefect of Zezhou, were ordered to garrison Wa Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan was recalled; Li Shaoqin, military governor of Taining, and Dong Zhang, prefect of Zezhou, were ordered to hold Wa Bridge.

sentences.zh: 李繼曮見唐甲兵之盛，歸，語岐王，岐王益懼。

translations.literal: Li Jiyan, having seen the strength of Tang armor and troops, returned and told the Prince of Qi, who grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: After seeing how strong Tang forces were, Li Jiyan returned and told the Prince of Qi, who grew still more frightened.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，表請正籓臣之禮，優詔不許。

translations.literal: On the guichou day, he memorialized asking to observe the proper rites of a subject; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day he asked permission to observe the full rites owed a subject; a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 孔謙惡張憲之來，言於豆盧革曰：「錢穀細事，一健吏可辦耳。

translations.literal: Kong Qian, resenting Zhang Xian's arrival, said to Doulu Ge, "Money and grain are minor matters—a single capable clerk could handle them.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian, who resented Zhang Xian's appointment, told Doulu Ge, "Money and grain are petty business—any capable clerk could manage them.

sentences.zh: 魏都根本之地，顧不重乎！

translations.literal: The capital of Wei is the root of the realm—can it not be weighty!
translations.idiomatic: But the Wei capital is the foundation of the realm—surely that deserves more weight!

sentences.zh: 興唐尹王正言操守有餘，智力不足，必不得已，使之居朝廷，眾人輔之，猶愈於專委方面也。」

translations.literal: Wang Zhengyan, prefect of Xingtang, has integrity to spare but lacks ability; if there is no choice, let him remain at court with others to assist him—still better than entrusting everything to the provinces."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan, prefect of Xingtang, is scrupulous but not clever; if we must, keep him at court with others to help him—still better than handing everything to the provinces."

sentences.zh: 革為之言於崇韜，崇韜乃奏留張憲於東京。

translations.literal: Ge spoke of this to Chongtao, and Chongtao then memorialized to keep Zhang Xian at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ge repeated this to Chongtao, who memorialized to keep Zhang Xian at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以正方為租庸使。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day, Zhengyan was appointed commissioner of tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day, Zhengyan was made commissioner of tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 正言昏懦，謙利其易制故也。

translations.literal: Zhengyan was dull and timid; Qian favored him because he was easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan was muddle-headed and weak; Qian favored him because he was easy to manipulate.

sentences.zh: 李存審奏契丹去，復得新州。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen reported that the Khitan had departed and that Xinzhou had been recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen reported that the Khitan had withdrawn and Xinzhou had been recovered.

sentences.zh: 戊午，敕鹽鐵、度支、戶部三司並隸租庸使。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day, an edict placed the three bureaus of Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Households under the tax and corvée commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day, an edict placed the Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Households bureaus under the tax and corvée commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上遣皇弟存渥、皇子繼岌迎太后、太妃於晉陽，太妃曰：「陵廟在此，若相與俱行，歲時何人奉祀！」

translations.literal: The emperor sent his younger brother Cunwo and his son Jiji to welcome the empress dowager and consort dowager from Jinyang. The consort dowager said, "The imperial tombs and temples are here; if we all go together, who will perform the seasonal sacrifices!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent his brother Cunwo and his son Jiji to bring the empress dowager and consort dowager from Jinyang. The consort dowager said, "The imperial tombs and temples are here—if we all leave, who will tend the seasonal rites?"

sentences.zh: 遂留不來。

translations.literal: She therefore remained and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: She stayed behind and did not come.

sentences.zh: 太后至，庚申，上出迎於河陽；

translations.literal: When the empress dowager arrived, on the gengshen day the emperor went out to meet her at Heyang;
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager arrived, on the gengshen day the emperor went out to meet her at Heyang;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，從太后入洛陽。

translations.literal: on the xinyou day he entered Luoyang with the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: on the xinyou day he entered Luoyang with her.

sentences.zh: 二月，己巳朔，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the jisi new moon, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the jisi new moon, the emperor offered sacrifice at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 孔謙欲聚斂以求媚，凡赦文所蠲者，謙復徵之。

translations.literal: Kong Qian wished to levy taxes to win favor; whatever the amnesty text remitted, Qian collected again.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian wanted to squeeze revenue to curry favor; whatever the amnesty remitted, he taxed again.

sentences.zh: 自是每有詔令，人皆不信，百姓愁怨。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever there was an edict, no one believed it, and the common people were full of grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever an edict was issued, no one believed it, and the people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜初至汴、洛，頗受籓鎮饋遺，所親或諫之，崇韜曰：「吾位兼將相，祿賜巨萬，豈藉外財！

translations.literal: When Guo Chongtao first arrived at Bian and Luoyang, he accepted many gifts from the regional commands. Some close to him admonished him; Chongtao said, "My rank combines general and minister, my salary and gifts run to tens of thousands—why would I need outside wealth!
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Chongtao first reached Bian and Luoyang, he accepted lavish gifts from the regional commands. Advisers warned him, but he said, "I hold both civil and military rank and draw enormous salary and gifts—why would I need outside money?

sentences.zh: 但以偽梁之季，賄賂成風，今河南籓鎮，皆梁之舊臣，主上之仇讎也，若拒，其意能無懼乎！

translations.literal: But in the last days of false Liang, bribery had become custom; the Henan commands now are all former Liang ministers, the emperor's enemies—if I refuse, can their minds be without fear!
translations.idiomatic: In the last days of false Liang, bribery was the norm; the Henan commands are all former Liang ministers—the emperor's enemies. If I refuse their gifts, won't they only grow afraid?

sentences.zh: 吾特為國家藏之私室耳。」

translations.literal: I am only storing it for the state in my private quarters."
translations.idiomatic: I am only banking it for the state in my own house."

sentences.zh: 及將祀南郊，崇韜首獻勞軍錢十萬緡。

translations.literal: When the southern suburb sacrifice was about to be held, Chongtao was the first to present one hundred thousand strings in troop-reward money.
translations.idiomatic: As the southern suburb rites approached, Chongtao was first to present one hundred thousand strings for rewarding the troops.

sentences.zh: 先是，宦官勸帝分天下財賦為內外府，州縣上供者入外府，充經費，方鎮貢獻者入內府，充宴游及給賜左右。

translations.literal: Earlier, eunuchs had urged the emperor to divide the empire's revenues into inner and outer treasuries: what prefectures and counties submitted went to the outer treasury for routine expenses; what the regional commands presented went to the inner treasury for banquets, travel, and gifts to those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, eunuchs had persuaded the emperor to split revenues into inner and outer treasuries: county and prefecture tribute funded the outer treasury for routine expenses, while regional gifts filled the inner treasury for feasts, travel, and rewards for his attendants.

sentences.zh: 於是外府常虛竭無餘而內府山積。

translations.literal: Thus the outer treasury was often empty and exhausted while the inner treasury piled up like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The outer treasury was often bare while the inner treasury overflowed.

sentences.zh: 及有司辦郊祀，乏勞軍錢，崇韜言於上曰：「臣已傾家所有以所助大禮，願陛下亦出內府之財以賜有司。」

translations.literal: When the offices prepared the suburban sacrifice and lacked troop-reward funds, Chongtao said to the emperor, "Your servant has emptied his household to assist the great rite; I hope Your Majesty will also draw on the inner treasury to supply the offices."
translations.idiomatic: When the rites office prepared the suburban sacrifice and lacked reward money, Chongtao told the emperor, "I have emptied my household to support the great ceremony; I hope Your Majesty will also draw on the inner treasury for the officials."

sentences.zh: 上默然久之，曰：「吾晉陽自有儲積，可令租庸輦取以相助。」

translations.literal: The emperor was silent a long while, then said, "I have stores of my own at Jinyang; let the tax commissioner cart them here to help."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent a long while, then said, "I have my own stores at Jinyang—have the tax commissioner cart them here."

sentences.zh: 於是取李崇韜私第金帛數十萬以益之，軍士皆不滿望，始怨恨，有離心矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon several hundred thousand in gold and silk from Li Chongtao's private residence were taken to supplement it; the soldiers were all disappointed in their expectations, and resentment and disaffection began.
translations.idiomatic: They then seized several hundred thousand in gold and silk from Li Chongtao's private residence to make up the sum. The soldiers felt cheated, resentment spread, and loyalty began to fray.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使李繼麟請榷安邑、解縣鹽，每季輸省課。

translations.literal: Li Jilin, military governor of Hezhong, asked to monopolize the salt of Anyi and Jie counties and remit provincial dues each quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jilin, military governor of Hezhong, asked to monopolize salt production at Anyi and Jie and remit provincial dues each quarter.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以繼麟充制置兩池榷鹽使。

translations.literal: On the jimao day, Jilin was appointed commissioner for regulating the salt of the two pools.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day, Jilin was made commissioner for regulating the two salt pools.

sentences.zh: 辛己，進岐王爵為秦王，仍不名、不拜。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day, the Prince of Qi's title was advanced to Prince of Qin, still without being named or required to bow.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day, the Prince of Qi was promoted to Prince of Qin, still addressed without personal name and exempt from bowing.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜知李紹宏怏怏，乃置內句使，掌句三司財賦，以紹宏為之，冀弭其意，而紹宏終不悅，徒使州縣增移報之煩。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao, knowing Li Shaohong was discontent, established the inner tally commissioner to oversee the tallying of the three bureaus' revenues and appointed Shaohong to it, hoping to appease him; but Shaohong remained displeased, and counties and prefectures were only burdened with extra reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Li Shaohong was unhappy, Guo Chongtao created the inner tally commissioner to oversee the three bureaus' accounts and gave the post to Shaohong, hoping to placate him—but Shaohong stayed sour, and counties and prefectures gained only more paperwork.

sentences.zh: 崇韜位兼將相，復領節旄，以天下為己任，權侔人主，旦夕車馬填門。

translations.literal: Chongtao held both civil and military rank and again bore a commander's baton; he took the realm as his charge, his power rivaling the sovereign's, and morning and evening his gate was choked with carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao held civil and military rank and again bore a commander's baton; he treated the realm as his own charge, wielded power equal to the throne, and his gate was jammed with visitors day and night.

sentences.zh: 性剛急，遇事輒發，嬖倖僥求，多所摧仰，宦官疾之，朝夕短之於上。

translations.literal: His nature was harsh and impatient; he erupted at every matter. Favorites who sought favors he often crushed; the eunuchs hated him and morning and evening slandered him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was harsh and quick-tempered, exploding at every issue. He crushed favorites who sought favors; the eunuchs hated him and whispered against him to the emperor morning and night.

sentences.zh: 崇韜扼腕，欲制之不能。

translations.literal: Chongtao wrung his hands, wishing to restrain them but unable.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao clenched his fists in frustration, unable to bring them to heel.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革、韋說嘗問之曰：「汾陽王本太原人徙華陰，公世家雁門，豈其枝派邪？」

translations.literal: Doulu Ge and Wei Shuo once asked him, "The Prince of Fenyang was originally a Taiyuan man who moved to Huayin; your clan has long been from Yanmen—are you perhaps of the same branch?"
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Ge and Wei Shuo once asked him, "The Prince of Fenyang was a Taiyuan native who moved to Huayin, while your family has long been from Yanmen—might you be of the same lineage?"

sentences.zh: 崇韜因曰：「遭亂，亡失譜諜，嘗聞先人言，上距汾陽世四耳。」

translations.literal: Chongtao therefore said, "In the turmoil the genealogy was lost, but I once heard the elders say we are only four generations from Fenyang."
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao replied, "The genealogy was lost in the chaos, but elders told me we are only four generations removed from Fenyang."

sentences.zh: 革曰：「然則固從祖也。」

translations.literal: Ge said, "Then he is indeed your collateral ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "Then he is your collateral ancestor, surely."

sentences.zh: 崇韜由是以膏梁自處，多甄別流品，引拔浮華，鄙棄勳舊。

translations.literal: Chongtao thereafter conducted himself as gentry, discriminating much by pedigree, promoting the flashy, and despising the meritorious veterans.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Chongtao acted the grandee, sorting men by pedigree, promoting the flashy, and scorning the old soldiers of merit.

sentences.zh: 有求官者，崇韜曰：「深知公功能，然門地寒素，不敢相用，恐為名流所嗤。」

translations.literal: When someone sought office, Chongtao would say, "I know well your ability, but your family standing is humble; I dare not employ you, fearing the leading figures would mock me."
translations.idiomatic: When men sought office, Chongtao would say, "I know your talent, but your family is too humble—I dare not appoint you, lest the elite laugh at me."

sentences.zh: 由是嬖倖疾之於內，勳舊怨之於外。

translations.literal: Because of this favorites hated him within and meritorious veterans resented him without.
translations.idiomatic: Favorites hated him at court; meritorious veterans resented him in the field.

sentences.zh: 崇韜屢請以樞密使讓李紹宏，上不許；

translations.literal: Chongtao repeatedly asked to yield the post of commissioner of military affairs to Li Shaohong; the emperor would not allow it;
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao repeatedly offered to yield the military affairs commission to Li Shaohong, but the emperor refused;

sentences.zh: 又請分樞密院事歸內諸司以輕其權，而宦官謗之不已。

translations.literal: he also asked to divide the Military Affairs Bureau's duties among the inner bureaus to lighten his power, while the eunuchs slandered him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to split Military Affairs Bureau duties among the inner bureaus to reduce his power, while the eunuchs never stopped slandering him.

sentences.zh: 崇韜鬱鬱不得志，與所親謀赴本鎮以避之，其人曰：「不可，蛟龍失水，螻蟻足以制之。」

translations.literal: Chongtao, depressed and unfulfilled, plotted with those close to him to go to his home command to escape; one said, "You must not—when a dragon leaves the water, even ants are enough to master it."
translations.idiomatic: Depressed and thwarted, Chongtao plotted with confidants to return to his home command to escape; one warned, "You must not—a dragon out of water can be mastered by ants."

sentences.zh: 先是，上欲以劉夫人為皇后，而有正妃韓夫人在，太后素惡劉夫人，崇韜亦屢諫，上以是不果。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had wished to make Lady Liu empress, but the legitimate consort Lady Han was present; the empress dowager had long disliked Lady Liu, and Chongtao had also admonished repeatedly—therefore it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had wanted to make Lady Liu empress, but legitimate consort Lady Han was still alive; the empress dowager had long disliked Lady Liu, and Chongtao had repeatedly objected—so the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 於是所親說崇韜曰：「公若請立劉夫人為皇后，上必喜。

translations.literal: Then those close to him urged Chongtao, "If you petition to establish Lady Liu as empress, the emperor will surely be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Confidants then urged Chongtao, "If you petition to make Lady Liu empress, the emperor will be delighted.

sentences.zh: 內有皇后之助，則伶宦輩不能為患矣。」

translations.literal: With the empress's help within, then the actors and eunuchs cannot become a scourge."
translations.idiomatic: With the empress behind you, the actors and eunuchs cannot harm you."

sentences.zh: 崇韜從之，與宰相帥百官共奏劉夫人宜正位中宮。

translations.literal: Chongtao followed this advice and, with the chief ministers leading all officials, jointly memorialized that Lady Liu should take the central palace position.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao took the advice and, with the chief ministers leading the officials, jointly memorialized that Lady Liu should be empress.

sentences.zh: 癸未，立魏國夫人劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the guimao day, Lady Liu, Duchess of Wei, was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, Lady Liu, Duchess of Wei, was made empress.

sentences.zh: 皇后生於寒微，既貴，專務蓄財，其在魏州，至於薪蘇果茹皆販鬻之。

translations.literal: The empress was born in humble circumstances; once elevated, she devoted herself to amassing wealth. While at Weizhou she even sold firewood, fruit, and vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Born in humble circumstances, once elevated she devoted herself to hoarding wealth; at Weizhou she had even sold firewood, fruit, and vegetables.

sentences.zh: 及為後，四方貢獻皆分為二，一上天子，一上中宮。

translations.literal: Once she was empress, tribute from the four directions was all divided in two—half to the Son of Heaven, half to the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: As empress, every regional tribute was split in two—half for the emperor, half for her.

sentences.zh: 以是寶貨山積，惟用寫佛經，施尼師而已。

translations.literal: Thus treasures piled like mountains; she used them only to copy Buddhist scriptures and give to nuns.
translations.idiomatic: Treasures piled up like mountains; she spent them only on copying sutras and gifts to nuns.

sentences.zh: 是時皇太后誥，皇后教，與制敕交行於籓鎮，奉之如一。

translations.literal: At this time edicts of the empress dowager and instructions of the empress circulated among the regional commands together with imperial orders, all obeyed alike.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts of the empress dowager and instructions of the empress now circulated among the commands alongside imperial orders, and all were obeyed equally.

sentences.zh: 詔蔡州刺史朱勍浚索水，通漕運。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhu Qin, prefect of Caizhou, to dredge the Suo River and open grain transport by canal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhu Qin, prefect of Caizhou, to dredge the Suo River and open the canal for grain transport.

sentences.zh: 三月，己亥朔，蜀主宴近臣於怡神亭，酒酣，君臣及宮人皆脫冠露髻，喧嘩自恣。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the jihai new moon, the lord of Shu feasted his close ministers at the Pleasing Spirit Pavilion; when the wine was deep, ruler and subjects and palace women all removed caps and bared their hair, shouting and reveling at will.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the jihai new moon, the lord of Shu feasted his close ministers at the Pleasing Spirit Pavilion; deep in wine, ruler, courtiers, and palace women threw off caps and let down their hair, shouting and carousing without restraint.

sentences.zh: 知制誥京兆李龜禎諫曰：「君臣沉湎，不憂國政，臣恐啟北敵之謀。」

translations.literal: Li Guizhen of Jingzhao, drafter of edicts, admonished, "Ruler and subjects are sunk in drink and heed not state affairs; your servant fears this will invite plotting by the northern enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Li Guizhen of Jingzhao, drafter of edicts, warned, "Court and throne are drowning in wine and ignoring government—I fear this will invite the northern enemy's designs."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The warning went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，鎮州言契丹將犯塞，詔橫海節度使李紹斌、北京左廂馬軍指揮使李從珂帥騎兵分道備之；

translations.literal: On the yisi day, Zhenzhou reported that the Khitan were about to raid the frontier; an edict ordered Li Shaobin, military governor of Henghai, and Li Congke, commander of the left wing cavalry of the northern capital, each to lead cavalry by separate routes to prepare;
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day, Zhenzhou reported an imminent Khitan raid; Li Shaobin, military governor of Henghai, and Li Congke, commander of the northern capital's left-wing cavalry, were ordered to prepare along separate routes;

sentences.zh: 天平節度使李嗣源屯邢州。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan, military governor of Tianping, encamped at Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan, military governor of Tianping, encamped at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹斌本姓趙，名行實，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Shaobin was originally surnamed Zhao, personal name Xingshi, a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin was born Zhao Xingshi of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，加高季興兼尚書令，時封南平王。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day, Gao Jixing was additionally appointed chief minister; he was then enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day, Gao Jixing was also made chief minister; he was then Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 李存審自以身為諸將之首，不得預克汴之功，感憤，疾益甚，屢表求入覲，郭崇韜抑而不許。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen, considering himself foremost among the generals yet denied a share in the capture of Bian, was moved to resentment; his illness grew worse and he repeatedly memorialized asking to attend court, but Guo Chongtao suppressed the requests and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen, who regarded himself foremost among the generals yet had been denied a role in taking Bian, brooded on the slight; his illness worsened and he repeatedly asked to attend court, but Guo Chongtao blocked every request.

sentences.zh: 存審疾亟，表乞生睹龍顏，乃許之。

translations.literal: When Cunshen's illness became critical, he memorialized begging to behold the dragon countenance while still alive, and only then was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Cunshen grew critically ill, he begged to see the emperor's face while he still lived—and only then was permission granted.

sentences.zh: 初，帝嘗與右武衛上將軍李存賢手搏，存賢不盡其技，帝曰：「汝能勝我，我當授籓鎮。」

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had once wrestled hand to hand with Li Cunxian, general of the Right Martial Guard; Cunxian did not use his full skill. The emperor said, "If you can defeat me, I will grant you a regional command."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had wrestled Li Cunxian, general of the Right Martial Guard; Cunxian held back. The emperor said, "Beat me and I will give you a regional command."

sentences.zh: 存賢乃奉詔，僅僕帝而止。

translations.literal: Cunxian then obeyed the command, barely threw the emperor down, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxian then obeyed, barely threw the emperor down, and stopped.

sentences.zh: 及許存審入覲，帝以存賢為盧龍行軍司馬，旬日除節度使，曰：「手搏之約，吾不食言矣。」

translations.literal: When Cunshen was permitted to attend court, the emperor made Cunxian chief of staff for the Luolong campaign; within ten days he was appointed military governor, and the emperor said, "The wrestling bargain—I do not break my word."
translations.idiomatic: When Cunshen was allowed to attend court, the emperor made Cunxian chief of staff for the Luolong campaign; within ten days he was appointed military governor. "The wrestling bargain," the emperor said, "I do not break my word."

sentences.zh: 庚戌，幽州奏契丹寇新城。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day, Youzhou reported that the Khitan were raiding Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, Youzhou reported Khitan raids on Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 勳臣畏伶宦之讒，皆不自安，蕃漢內外馬步副總管李嗣源求解兵柄，帝不許。

translations.literal: Meritorious ministers, fearing slander by actors and eunuchs, were all ill at ease; Li Siyuan, deputy overall commander of Han and non-Han horse and foot forces within and without, asked to be relieved of military authority, but the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ministers, fearing slander from actors and eunuchs, grew uneasy; Li Siyuan, deputy overall commander of all Han and non-Han forces, asked to surrender military authority, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 自唐末喪亂，搢紳之家或以告赤鬻於族姻，遂亂昭穆，至有舅叔拜甥、侄者，選人偽濫者眾。

translations.literal: Since the disorders at the end of Tang, gentry families sometimes sold mourning notices to kin by marriage, thus confusing senior and junior lines, until uncles bowed to nephews and nieces; many candidates were fraudulent.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, gentry families sometimes sold mourning notices to in-laws, scrambling genealogies until uncles bowed to nephews; office-seekers were rife with fraud.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜欲革其弊，請令銓司精加考核。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao wished to reform this abuse and asked that the selection office conduct rigorous examination.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao sought to end the abuse and ordered the selection office to examine candidates rigorously.

sentences.zh: 時南郊行事官千二百人，注官者才數十人，塗毀告身者十之九。

translations.literal: At that time there were twelve hundred officers for the southern suburb rites; only several dozen received appointment, and nine-tenths defaced their commission documents.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve hundred men were slated for the southern suburb rites, but only a few dozen were approved; nine in ten defaced their appointment documents.

sentences.zh: 選人或號哭道路，或餒死逆旅。

translations.literal: Some candidates wailed in the roads; others starved to death at inns.
translations.idiomatic: Some candidates wailed in the streets; others starved at roadside inns.

sentences.zh: 唐室諸陵先為溫韜所發，庚申，以工部郎中李途為長安按視諸陵使。

translations.literal: The tombs of the Tang house had earlier been opened by Wen Tao; on the gengshen day, Li Tu, bureau director in the Ministry of Works, was made commissioner to inspect all tombs at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tang imperial tombs had already been looted by Wen Tao; on the gengshen day Li Tu of the Ministry of Works was sent to inspect all tombs at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 皇子繼岌代張全義判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: The prince Jiji replaced Zhang Quanyi in overseeing the Six Armies and palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiji replaced Zhang Quanyi as overseer of the Six Armies and palace guards.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己巳朔，群臣上尊號曰昭文睿武至德光孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the jisi new moon, the officials presented the honorific title Illustrious in Culture, Sagacious in Warfare, Supreme in Virtue, Radiant in Filial Piety Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the jisi new moon, officials offered the honorific Illustrious in Culture, Sagacious in Warfare, Supreme in Virtue, Radiant in Filial Piety Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝遣客省使李嚴使於蜀，嚴盛稱帝威德，有混一天下之志。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Li Yan of the Reception Bureau as envoy to Shu; Yan lavishly praised the emperor's majesty and virtue and spoke of his ambition to unify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Yan of the Reception Bureau to Shu; Yan lavishly praised the emperor's power and declared his ambition to reunify the realm.

sentences.zh: 且言朱氏篡竊，諸侯曾無勤王之舉。

translations.literal: He also said the Zhu clan had usurped the throne and that the feudal lords had never raised troops to rescue the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: He also said the Zhu had usurped the throne while the regional lords never stirred to defend the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 王宗儔以其語侵蜀，請斬之，蜀主不從。

translations.literal: Wang Zongchou, because his words insulted Shu, asked that he be executed; the lord of Shu did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongchou, taking the speech as an insult to Shu, asked that Yan be executed, but the lord of Shu refused.

sentences.zh: 宣徽北院使宋光葆上言：「晉王有憑陵我國家之志，宜選將練兵，屯戍邊鄙，積糗糧，治戰艦以待之。」

translations.literal: Song Guangbao, commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, memorialized, "The Prince of Jin intends to bully our state; we should select generals, train troops, garrison the frontier, stock dry provisions, and build warships to await him."
translations.idiomatic: Song Guangbao of the northern Palace Secretariat bureau memorialized, "The Prince of Jin means to overrun us—we should pick generals, drill troops, garrison the borders, stock provisions, and build warships to meet him."

sentences.zh: 蜀主乃以光葆為梓州觀察使，充武德節度留後。

translations.literal: The lord of Shu then made Guangbao observation commissioner of Zizhou and acting military governor of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Shu then made Guangbao observation commissioner of Zizhou and acting military governor of Wude.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，加楚王殷兼尚書令。

translations.literal: On the yihai day, Prince Yin of Chu was additionally appointed chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day, Prince Yin of Chu was also made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，賜前保義留後霍彥威姓名李紹真。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day, the former acting prefect of Baoyi, Huo Yanwei, was granted the surname and personal name Li Shaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day, former Baoyi acting prefect Huo Yanwei was given the name Li Shaozhen.

sentences.zh: 秦忠敬王李茂貞卒，遣奏以其子繼曮權知鳳翔軍府事。

translations.literal: Prince Zhongjing of Qin, Li Maozhen, died; a memorial was sent asking that his son Jiyan temporarily oversee Fengxiang army headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen, Prince Zhongjing of Qin, died; his son Jiyan was reported to be temporarily overseeing Fengxiang headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，安義牙將楊立有寵於李繼韜，繼韜誅，常邑邑思亂。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Li, a guard officer of Anyi, had been favored by Li Jitao; when Jitao was executed, Li often brooded and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Anyi guard officer Yang Li had been favored by Li Jitao; after Jitao's execution, Yang brooded and plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 會發安義兵三千戍涿州，立謂其眾曰：「前此潞兵未嘗戍邊，今朝廷驅我輩投之絕塞，蓋不欲置之潞州耳。

translations.literal: When three thousand Anyi troops were sent to garrison Zhuozhou, Li told his men, "Lu troops have never before garrisoned the frontier; now the court drives us to the far border—surely it does not wish us to remain at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When three thousand Anyi troops were sent to garrison Zhuozhou, Yang told his men, "Lu soldiers have never been posted to the frontier—the court is sending us to the ends of the earth because it does not want us back in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 與其暴骨沙場，不若據城自守，事成富貴，不成為群盜耳。」

translations.literal: Rather than leave our bones on the battlefield, better to hold the city: if we succeed, wealth and honor; if not, we become bandits together."
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold the city than die on some frontier field—if we win, we are rich; if we lose, we are bandits together."

sentences.zh: 因聚噪攻子城東門，焚掠市肆；

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered, shouting, attacked the east gate of the inner city, and burned and plundered the markets;
translations.idiomatic: They rallied, stormed the inner city's east gate, and burned and looted the markets;

sentences.zh: 節度副使李繼珂、監軍張弘祚棄城走，立自稱留後，遣將士表求旌節。

translations.literal: the deputy military governor Li Jike and army supervisor Zhang Hongzuo abandoned the city and fled; Li declared himself acting prefect and sent officers to memorialize for the commander's baton.
translations.idiomatic: deputy military governor Li Jike and army supervisor Zhang Hongzuo fled; Yang declared himself acting prefect and petitioned for imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 詔以天平節度使李嗣源為招討使，武寧節度使李紹榮為部署，帳前都指揮使張廷蘊為馬步都指揮使以討之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Li Siyuan, military governor of Tianping, as campaign commander; Li Shaorong, military governor of Wuning, as deputy commander; and Zhang Tingyun, overall commander before the tent, as overall horse and foot commander to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan of Tianping was made campaign commander, Li Shaorong of Wuning deputy commander, and Zhang Tingyun overall horse and foot commander to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 孔謙貸民錢，使以賤估償絲，屢檄州縣督之。

translations.literal: Kong Qian lent money to the people and made them repay in silk at low valuation, repeatedly dispatching orders to prefectures and counties to enforce it.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian lent money to commoners and forced repayment in silk at cut-rate prices, repeatedly ordering prefectures and counties to enforce collection.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨、權知汴州盧質上言：「梁趙巖為租庸使，舉貸誅斂，結怨於人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, chief Hanlin academician and acting prefect of Bianzhou, memorialized, "When Zhao Yan of Liang was tax commissioner, he lent money and extorted, earning people's hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, chief Hanlin academician and acting prefect of Bianzhou, wrote, "When Zhao Yan of Liang ran tax affairs, he lent money and extorted until the people hated him.

sentences.zh: 陛下革故鼎新，為人除害，而有司未改其所為，是趙巖復生也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has renewed the realm and removed harm for the people, yet the offices have not changed their ways—this is Zhao Yan reborn.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty renewed the realm and cleared away such harm, yet the offices act unchanged—Zhao Yan has been reborn.

sentences.zh: 今春霜害桑，繭絲甚薄，但輸正稅，猶懼流移，況益以稱貸，人何以堪！

translations.literal: This spring frost harmed the mulberries and cocoon silk is very thin; paying only regular taxes, we still fear displacement—how much less when forced loans are added! How can the people bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Spring frost ruined the mulberries and silk is poor; people can barely pay regular taxes without fleeing—how can they bear forced loans on top?

sentences.zh: 臣惟事天子，不事租庸，敕旨未頒，省牒頻下，願早降明命！」

translations.literal: Your servant serves only the Son of Heaven, not the tax commissioner; imperial edicts have not been issued, yet provincial orders come repeatedly—I beg an early clear command!"
translations.idiomatic: I serve the Son of Heaven, not the tax commissioner—no imperial edict has come, yet provincial orders rain down. I beg a clear command at once!"

sentences.zh: 帝不報。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 漢主引兵侵閩，屯於汀、漳境上；

translations.literal: The lord of Han led troops to invade Min and encamped on the Ting and Zhang frontier;
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Han invaded Min and encamped on the Ting and Zhang border;

sentences.zh: 閩人擊之，漢主敗走。

translations.literal: the people of Min struck them and the lord of Han was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Min forces routed him and he fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 初，胡柳之役，伶人周匝為梁所得，帝每思之；

translations.literal: Earlier, at the battle of Huliu, the actor Zhou Za had been captured by Liang; the emperor often thought of him;
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Huliu, the actor Zhou Za had been captured by Liang, and the emperor often missed him;

sentences.zh: 入汴之日，匝謁見於馬前，帝甚喜。

translations.literal: on the day of entering Bian, Za paid his respects before the horse and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: on the day Bian fell, Za greeted him before his horse and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 匝涕泣言曰：「臣所以得生全者，皆梁教坊使陳俊、內園栽接使儲德源之力也，願就陛下乞二州以報之。」

translations.literal: Za wept and said, "Your servant owes his life to Chen Jun, commissioner of the Liang music office, and Chu Deyuan, commissioner of inner-garden planting—I beg Your Majesty for two prefectures to repay them."
translations.idiomatic: Za wept and said, "I owe my life to Chen Jun of the Liang music office and Chu Deyuan of the inner gardens—I beg two prefectures from Your Majesty to repay them."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜諫曰：「陛下所與共取天下者，皆英豪忠勇之士。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao admonished, "Those with whom Your Majesty took the realm are all heroic, loyal, and brave men.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao objected, "Those who won the realm with Your Majesty are heroic, loyal soldiers.

sentences.zh: 今大功始就，封賞未及一人，而先以伶人為刺史，恐失天下心。」

translations.literal: Now the great achievement is barely won and not one man has yet received enfeoffment or reward, yet actors are first made prefects—I fear you will lose the hearts of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The great victory is barely won and not one man has been rewarded, yet actors are made prefects first—you will lose the realm's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 以是不行。

translations.literal: Therefore it did not go through.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments did not go through.

sentences.zh: 逾年，伶人屢以為言，帝謂崇韜曰：「吾已許周匝矣，使吾慚見此三人。

translations.literal: After more than a year the actors repeatedly spoke of it; the emperor told Chongtao, "I have already promised Zhou Za—how can I face these three men in shame?
translations.idiomatic: A year later the actors kept pressing; the emperor told Chongtao, "I promised Zhou Za—how can I face those three men in shame?

sentences.zh: 公言雖正，然當為我屈意行之。」

translations.literal: Your words are correct, but you must bend your will for me and carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: You are right, but bend your will for me and do it."

sentences.zh: 五月，壬寅，以俊為景州刺史，德源為憲州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the renyin day, Jun was made prefect of Jingzhou and Deyuan prefect of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the renyin day, Jun became prefect of Jingzhou and Deyuan prefect of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時親軍有從帝百戰未得刺史者，莫不憤歎。

translations.literal: At that time among the imperial guard were many who had fought a hundred battles with the emperor yet received no prefecture—all were indignant and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the imperial guard who had fought a hundred battles with the emperor still had no prefecture—all groaned in anger.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，右諫議大夫薛昭文上疏，以為：「諸道僭竊者尚多，征伐之謀，未可遽息。

translations.literal: On the yisi day, Xue Zhaowen, right remonstrance grandee, submitted a memorial stating, "Usurpers remain numerous among the circuits; plans for campaigns must not be hastily set aside.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day, Xue Zhaowen, right remonstrance grandee, wrote, "Many circuits still have usurpers—campaign plans must not be dropped yet.

sentences.zh: 又，士卒久從征伐，賞給未豐，貧乏者多，宜以四方貢獻及南郊羨餘，更加頒賚。

translations.literal: Moreover, soldiers have long followed campaigns yet rewards are not ample; many are destitute—tribute from the four directions and surplus from the southern suburb rites should be used for further distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, soldiers have campaigned for years with thin rewards—many are poor. Use tribute from the regions and surplus from the southern suburb rites for further gifts.

sentences.zh: 又，河南諸軍皆梁之精銳，恐僭竊之國潛以厚利誘之，宜加收撫。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Henan armies are all Liang's elite; I fear usurping states may secretly lure them with rich profit—they should be won over more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Henan armies are Liang's elite—usurpers may secretly bribe them. Win them over more carefully.

sentences.zh: 又，戶口流亡者，宜寬徭薄賦以安集之。

translations.literal: Moreover, for households that have fled, corvée should be eased and taxes lightened to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, ease corvée and lighten taxes to settle refugees.

sentences.zh: 又，土木不急之役，宜加裁省。

translations.literal: Moreover, non-urgent construction projects should be further cut.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, cut non-urgent construction.

sentences.zh: 又請擇隙地牧馬，勿使踐京畿民田。」

translations.literal: He also asked to choose open land for pasturing horses and not let them trample the people's fields in the capital region."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to pasture horses on open land so they would not trample capital-region farmland."

sentences.zh: 皆不從。

translations.literal: None was followed.
translations.idiomatic: None of it was heeded.

sentences.zh: 戊申，蜀主遣李嚴還。

translations.literal: On the wushen day, the lord of Shu sent Li Yan back.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, the lord of Shu sent Li Yan home.

sentences.zh: 初，帝因嚴入蜀，令以馬市宮中珍玩，而蜀法禁錦綺珍奇不得入中國，其粗惡者乃聽入中國，謂之「入草物」。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor, through Yan's mission to Shu, had ordered horses traded for palace treasures; but Shu law forbade brocades and curios from entering China—only coarse goods were allowed in, called "grass-entry goods."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had sent Yan to trade horses for palace treasures, but Shu law barred brocades and curios from China—only coarse goods were allowed, called "grass-entry goods."

sentences.zh: 嚴還，以聞，帝怒曰：「王衍寧免為入草之人乎！」

translations.literal: When Yan returned and reported this, the emperor raged, "Can Wang Yan escape being a grass-entry man!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan reported this, the emperor raged, "Does Wang Yan think he can treat me like grass-entry goods!"

sentences.zh: 嚴因言於帝曰：「衍童騃荒縱，不親政務，斥遠故老，暱比小人。

translations.literal: Yan then told the emperor, "Yan is childish, foolish, and dissolute, does not attend to government, drives off old ministers, and clings to petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then told the emperor, "Wang Yan is childish and dissolute, ignores government, drives off elders, and favors petty men.

sentences.zh: 其用事之臣王宗弼、宋光嗣等，諂諛專恣，黷貨無厭，賢愚易位，刑賞紊亂，君臣上下專以奢淫相尚。

translations.literal: His ministers in power, Wang Zongbi, Song Guangsi, and others, are flattering, domineering, and insatiable in bribes; worthy and base change places, punishments and rewards are chaotic, and ruler and subjects alike vie only in luxury and debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers Wang Zongbi and Song Guangsi flatter and dominate, take endless bribes, reverse merit and folly, scramble rewards and punishments, and court and throne compete only in luxury.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，大兵一臨，瓦解土崩，可翹足而待也。」

translations.literal: In your servant's view, when great armies arrive they will collapse like tiles and earth—you may wait with foot raised."
translations.idiomatic: In my view, when your armies arrive they will crumble—you need only wait."

sentences.zh: 帝深以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝以潞州叛故，庚戌，詔天下州鎮無得修城浚隍，悉毀防城之具。

translations.literal: Because of the Luzhou rebellion, on the gengxu day the emperor ordered that no prefecture or command might repair walls or deepen moats, and all defensive equipment was to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Luzhou revolt, on the gengxu day he ordered every command to stop fortifying walls and moats and to destroy all defensive gear.

sentences.zh: 壬子，新宣武節度使兼中書令、蕃漢馬步總管李存審卒於幽州。

translations.literal: On the renzi day, Li Cunshen, newly appointed military governor of Xuanwu and chief minister, overall commander of Han and non-Han horse and foot forces, died at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day, Li Cunshen, newly made military governor of Xuanwu, chief minister, and overall commander of Han and non-Han forces, died at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 存審出於寒微，常戒諸子曰：「爾父少提一劍去鄉里，四十年間，位極將相，其間出萬死獲一生者非一，破骨出鏃者凡百餘。」

translations.literal: Cunshen came from humble origins and often warned his sons, "Your father left home young with a single sword; in forty years he reached the summit of general and minister. More than once he escaped ten thousand deaths for one life; arrowheads taken from broken bone number over a hundred."
translations.idiomatic: Born humble, Cunshen often told his sons, "Your father left home with one sword; in forty years he rose to general and minister, cheated death again and again, and had more than a hundred arrowheads cut from his bones."

sentences.zh: 因授以所出鏃，命藏之，曰：「爾曹生於膏梁，當知爾父起家如此也。」

translations.literal: He then handed them the extracted arrowheads and ordered them kept, saying, "You were born to luxury—you should know your father rose thus."
translations.idiomatic: He gave them the arrowheads to keep, saying, "You were born to comfort—you should know how your father rose."

sentences.zh: 幽州言契丹將入寇，甲寅，以橫海節度使李紹斌充東北面行營招討使，將大軍渡河而北。

translations.literal: Youzhou reported that the Khitan were about to invade; on the jiayin day, Li Shaobin, military governor of Henghai, was made eastern-northern campaign commander and led a great army across the river northward.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou reported an imminent Khitan invasion; on the jiayin day Li Shaobin of Henghai was made eastern-northern campaign commander and led a great army north across the river.

sentences.zh: 契丹屯幽州東南城門之外，虜騎充斥，饋運多為所掠。

translations.literal: The Khitan encamped outside Youzhou's southeast gate; enemy cavalry filled the land and supply convoys were largely plundered.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan camped outside Youzhou's southeast gate; enemy horsemen swarmed the roads and supply trains were largely looted.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以李繼曮為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: On the renxu day, Li Jiyan was made military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day, Li Jiyan was made military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以權知歸義留後曹義金為節度使。

translations.literal: On the yichou day, Cao Yijin, acting prefect of Guiyi, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, acting Guiyi prefect Cao Yijin was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 時瓜、沙與吐蕃雜居，義金遣使間道入貢，故命之。

translations.literal: At that time Guazhou and Shazhou lived mixed with Tibetans; Yijin sent envoys by secret routes to present tribute, hence the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Guazhou and Shazhou then lived mixed with Tibetans; Yijin had sent envoys by secret routes with tribute, hence the appointment.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源大軍前鋒至潞州，日已暝；

translations.literal: The vanguard of Li Siyuan's great army reached Luzhou as the sun was setting;
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan's vanguard reached Luzhou at dusk;

sentences.zh: 泊軍方定，張廷蘊帥麾下壯士百餘輩逾塹坎城而上，守者不能御，即斬關延諸軍入。

translations.literal: when the army had just settled, Zhang Tingyun led more than a hundred stalwarts over moat and wall; the defenders could not stop them, and he cut the gate bar and admitted the armies.
translations.idiomatic: as the army was settling in, Zhang Tingyun led a hundred picked men over moat and wall; defenders could not stop them, and he cut the bar and let the armies in.

sentences.zh: 比明，嗣源及李紹榮至，城已下矣，嗣源等不悅。

translations.literal: By dawn Siyuan and Li Shaorong arrived; the city was already taken, and Siyuan and the others were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Siyuan and Li Shaorong arrived to find the city already fallen—they were displeased.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，嗣源奏潞州平。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day, Siyuan reported Luzhou pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, Siyuan reported Luzhou pacified.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，磔楊立及其黨於鎮國橋。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the bingzi day, Yang Li and his partisans were dismembered at Zhenguo Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the bingzi day, Yang Li and his followers were dismembered at Zhenguo Bridge.

sentences.zh: 潞州城池高深，帝命夷之。

translations.literal: Luzhou's walls and moat were high and deep; the emperor ordered them leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou's walls and moat were high and deep; the emperor ordered them demolished.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以武寧節度使李紹榮為歸德節度使、同平章事，留宿衛，寵遇甚厚。

translations.literal: On the bingxu day, Li Shaorong, military governor of Wuning, was made military governor of Guide and associate chief minister, kept for palace guard duty, and favored very generously.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day, Li Shaorong of Wuning was made military governor of Guide and associate chief minister, kept at court for guard duty, and lavishly favored.

sentences.zh: 帝或時與太后，皇后同至其家。

translations.literal: The emperor sometimes came to his home together with the empress dowager and empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sometimes visited his home with the empress dowager and empress.

sentences.zh: 帝有幸姬，色美，嘗生子矣，劉後妒之。

translations.literal: The emperor had a favored consort, beautiful in appearance, who had borne a son; Empress Liu was jealous of her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a beautiful favored consort who had borne him a son; Empress Liu was jealous.

sentences.zh: 會紹榮喪妻，一日，侍禁中，帝問紹榮：「汝復娶乎？

translations.literal: When Shaorong's wife died, one day while attending in the palace the emperor asked Shaorong, "Will you marry again?
translations.idiomatic: When Shaorong's wife died, the emperor asked him one day at court, "Will you marry again?

sentences.zh: 為汝求婚。」

translations.literal: I will find a wife for you."
translations.idiomatic: I will find you a wife."

sentences.zh: 後因指幸姬曰：「大家憐紹榮，何不以此賜之！」

translations.literal: The empress then pointed at the favored consort and said, "His Majesty pities Shaorong—why not give her to him!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress pointed at the favored consort and said, "His Majesty pities Shaorong—why not give her to him!"

sentences.zh: 帝難言不可，微許之。

translations.literal: The emperor found it hard to say no and faintly assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not refuse aloud and faintly agreed.

sentences.zh: 後趣紹榮拜謝，比起，顧幸姬，已肩輿出宮矣。

translations.literal: The empress urged Shaorong to bow in thanks; when he rose and looked for the favored consort, she was already in a palanquin leaving the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress hurried Shaorong to bow thanks; when he rose and looked for the consort, she was already being carried out of the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝為之托疾不食者累日。

translations.literal: The emperor pretended illness and would not eat for many days because of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feigned illness and refused food for days.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以天平節度使李嗣源為宣武節度使，代李存審為蕃漢內外馬步總管。

translations.literal: On the renchen day, Li Siyuan, military governor of Tianping, was made military governor of Xuanwu, replacing Li Cunshen as overall commander of Han and non-Han horse and foot forces within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day, Li Siyuan of Tianping was made military governor of Xuanwu, replacing Li Cunshen as overall commander of all Han and non-Han forces.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬寅，蜀以禮部書許寂為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the renyin day, Shu made Xu Ji, vice minister of rites, vice director of the Secretariat and associate chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the renyin day, Shu made Xu Ji, vice minister of rites, vice director of the Secretariat and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 孔謙復短王正言於郭崇韜，又厚賂伶宦，求租庸使，終不獲，意怏怏，癸卯，表求解職。

translations.literal: Kong Qian again slandered Wang Zhengyan to Guo Chongtao and lavishly bribed actors and eunuchs seeking the tax commission, but never obtained it; resentful, on the guimao day he memorialized asking to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian again slandered Wang Zhengyan to Guo Chongtao and bribed actors and eunuchs for the tax commission but failed; on the guimao day he memorialized to resign in a sulk.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，以為避事，將置於法，景進救之，得免。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, thinking he was shirking duty, and was about to punish him by law; Jing Jin rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, thinking he was shirking duty, and was about to punish him; Jing Jin intervened and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 梁所決河連年為曹、濮患，甲辰，命右監門上將軍婁繼英督汴、滑兵塞之。

translations.literal: The breach in the Yellow River made by Liang had for years plagued Cao and Pu; on the jiachen day Lou Jiying, general of the Right Gate Guard, was ordered to supervise Bian and Hua troops in blocking it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River breach Liang had cut had plagued Cao and Pu for years; on the jiachen day Lou Jiying of the Right Gate Guard was ordered to supervise Bian and Hua troops in blocking it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復壞。

translations.literal: Before long it broke again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it broke again.

sentences.zh: 庚申，置威塞軍於新州。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day, the Weisai Army was established at Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day, the Weisai Army was established at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹恃其強盛，遣使就帝求幽州以處盧文進。

translations.literal: Relying on their strength, the Khitan sent envoys to the emperor asking for Youzhou to settle Lu Wenjin.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in their power, the Khitan asked the emperor for Youzhou to settle Lu Wenjin.

sentences.zh: 時東北諸夷皆役屬契丹，惟渤海未服；

translations.literal: At that time all northeastern tribes were subject to the Khitan except Bohai, which had not submitted;
translations.idiomatic: All northeastern tribes were subject to the Khitan except Bohai;

sentences.zh: 契丹主謀入寇，恐渤海掎其後，乃先舉兵擊渤海之遼東，遣其將禿餒及盧文進據營、平等州以擾燕地。

translations.literal: the Khitan ruler planned invasion but feared Bohai would strike from behind; he therefore first raised troops against Liaodong in Bohai and sent his general Tunei and Lu Wenjin to hold Ying and Ping prefectures to harass the Yan region.
translations.idiomatic: the Khitan ruler planned invasion but feared Bohai would strike his rear, so he first attacked Bohai's Liaodong and sent Tunei and Lu Wenjin to hold Ying and Ping and harass Yan.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊辰，蜀主以右定遠軍使王宗鍔為招討馬步使，帥二十一軍屯洋州；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the wuchen day, the lord of Shu made Wang Zong'e, commissioner of the Right Dingyuan Army, campaign horse and foot commander, leading twenty-one armies to encamp at Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the wuchen day, the lord of Shu made Wang Zong'e campaign horse and foot commander and posted twenty-one armies at Yangzhou;

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以長直馬軍使林思諤為昭武節度使，戍利州以備唐。

translations.literal: on the yihai day Lin Si'e, commissioner of the long-service cavalry, was made military governor of Zhaowu and garrisoned Lizhou to guard against Tang.
translations.idiomatic: on the yihai day Lin Si'e was made military governor of Zhaowu and garrisoned Lizhou against Tang.

sentences.zh: 租庸使王正言病風，恍惚不能治事，景進屢以為言。

translations.literal: Wang Zhengyan, tax commissioner, was ill with wind disorder and in a daze could not manage affairs; Jing Jin repeatedly spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioner Wang Zhengyan had a stroke and could barely work; Jing Jin kept complaining.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以副使、衛尉卿孔謙為租庸使，右威衛大將軍孔循為副使。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day, Kong Qian, deputy commissioner and minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was made tax commissioner, and Kong Xun, great general of the Right Weiwu Guard, deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, Kong Qian was made tax commissioner and Kong Xun, great general of the Right Weiwu Guard, his deputy.

sentences.zh: 循即趙殷衡也，梁亡，復其姓名。

translations.literal: Xun was Zhao Yinheng; when Liang perished his original name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was Zhao Yinheng; when Liang fell he recovered his original name.

sentences.zh: 謙自是得行其志，重斂急征以充帝欲，民不聊生。

translations.literal: From then on Qian could carry out his will, levying heavily and collecting urgently to fill the emperor's desires; the people could not live.
translations.idiomatic: Qian then had free rein, taxing heavily to fill the emperor's coffers until the people could not survive.

sentences.zh: 癸未，賜謙號豐財贍國功臣。

translations.literal: On the guiwei day, Qian was granted the title Meritorious in Enriching the State and Supplying the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day, Qian was titled Meritorious in Enriching the State and Supplying the Realm.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣使者李彥稠入蜀，九月，己亥，至成都。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent the envoy Li Yanchou to Shu; in the ninth month, on the jihai day, he reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Li Yanchou to Shu; in the ninth month, on the jihai day, he reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝獵於近郊。

translations.literal: On the guimao day, the emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, the emperor hunted near the capital.

sentences.zh: 時帝屢出遊獵，從騎傷民禾稼，洛陽令何澤付於叢薄，俟帝至，遮馬諫曰：「陛下賦斂既急，今稼穡將成，復蹂踐之，使吏何以為理，民何以為生！

translations.literal: The emperor often went out hunting; attendant horsemen damaged the people's crops. He Ze, magistrate of Luoyang, hid in the brush and, when the emperor arrived, blocked his horse and admonished, "Your Majesty's levies are already harsh; the crops are nearly ripe and are trampled again—how can officials govern, how can the people live!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hunted often and his escort trampled crops. Luoyang magistrate He Ze hid in the brush and, when the emperor came, blocked his horse: "Your levies are already harsh—the crops are nearly ripe and your riders trample them. How can officials govern? How can the people live?

sentences.zh: 臣願先賜死。」

translations.literal: Your servant begs to be executed first."
translations.idiomatic: Execute me first."

sentences.zh: 帝慰而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 澤，廣州人也。

translations.literal: Ze was a man of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was from Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹攻渤海，無功而還。

translations.literal: The Khitan attacked Bohai and returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan attacked Bohai and withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: 蜀前山南節度使兼中書令王宗儔以蜀主失德，與王宗弼謀廢立，宗弼猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Wang Zongchou, former military governor of Qianshan and chief minister, because the lord of Shu had lost virtue plotted with Wang Zongbi to depose and replace him; Zongbi hesitated and did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongchou, former Qianshan military governor and chief minister, believing the lord of Shu had lost virtue plotted with Wang Zongbi to depose him; Zongbi hesitated.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，宗儔憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day, Zongchou died of grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, Zongchou died of grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 宗弼謂樞密使宋光嗣、景潤澄等曰：「宗儔教我殺爾曹，今日無患矣。」

translations.literal: Zongbi told the military affairs commissioners Song Guangsi, Jing Runcheng, and others, "Zongchou urged me to kill you all—today you need have no fear."
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi told military affairs commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, "Zongchou wanted me to kill you—today you are safe."

sentences.zh: 光嗣輩俯伏泣謝。

translations.literal: Guangsi and the others prostrated themselves weeping in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi and the others prostrated themselves, weeping thanks.

sentences.zh: 宗弼子承班聞之，謂人曰：「吾家難乎免矣。」

translations.literal: Zongbi's son Chengban, hearing this, told others, "Our family will hardly escape disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi's son Chengban heard and said, "Our family will hardly escape ruin."

sentences.zh: 乙卯，蜀主以前鎮江軍節度使張武為峽路應援招討使。

translations.literal: On the yimao day, the lord of Shu made Zhang Wu, former military governor of Zhenjiang, relief campaign commander of the Gorges route.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day, the lord of Shu made former Zhenjiang military governor Zhang Wu relief campaign commander of the Gorges route.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，幽州言契丹入寇。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day, Youzhou reported that the Khitan had invaded.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day, Youzhou reported a Khitan incursion.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛未，天平節度使李存霸、平盧節度使符習言：「屬州多稱直奉租庸使貼指揮公事，使司殊不知，有紊規程。」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the xinwei day, Li Cunba, military governor of Tianping, and Fu Xi, military governor of Pinglu, said: "Subordinate prefectures frequently claim that posted orders from the tax and corvée commissioner on direct tribute matters bypass official channels, of which the commissioner's office knows nothing, disrupting proper procedure.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the xinwei day, Li Cunba, military governor of Tianping, and Fu Xi, military governor of Pinglu, reported: "Many subordinate prefectures say they receive posted orders from the tax and corvée commissioner on direct tribute matters without the commissioner's office knowing anything about them, which disrupts established procedure.

sentences.zh: 租庸使奏，近例皆直下。

translations.literal: The tax and corvée commissioner memorialized that recent practice was for orders to go directly down.
translations.idiomatic: The tax and corvée commissioner replied that recent practice had been to send orders straight to the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 敕：「朝廷故事，制敕不下支郡，牧守不專奏陳。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "According to court precedent, imperial edicts were not sent directly to subordinate prefectures, and prefects and governors were not to memorialize on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "By court precedent, imperial edicts were not sent straight to subordinate prefectures, and local governors were not to memorialize on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 今兩道所奏，乃本朝舊規；

translations.literal: What the two circuits have memorialized reflects our dynasty's old regulations;
translations.idiomatic: What the two circuits have reported reflects our dynasty's established rules;

sentences.zh: 租庸所陳，是偽廷近事。

translations.literal: what the tax and corvée commissioner stated reflects recent practices of the false regime.
translations.idiomatic: what the tax and corvée commissioner described reflects recent practices of the usurping court.

sentences.zh: 自今支郡自非進奉，皆須本道騰奏，租庸征催亦須牒觀察使。」

translations.literal: From now on, subordinate prefectures, unless making direct tribute, must report through their circuit; tax and corvée collection and demands must also go through memorials to the surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, unless making direct tribute, subordinate prefectures must report through their circuit, and tax and corvée collection must also be routed through the surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 雖有此敕，竟不行。

translations.literal: Although this edict was issued, it was never implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Despite the edict, it was never put into effect.

sentences.zh: 易定言契丹入寇。

translations.literal: Yiding reported that the Khitan had invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yiding reported a Khitan incursion.

sentences.zh: 蜀宣徽北院使王承休請擇諸軍驍勇者萬二千人，置駕下左、右龍武步騎四十軍，兵械給賜皆優異於它軍，以承休為龍武軍馬步都指揮使，以裨將安重霸副之，舊將無不憤恥。

translations.literal: Wang Chengyou, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Shu Palace Secretariat, asked to select twelve thousand of the fiercest troops from all armies, form forty Left and Right Dragon Martial infantry and cavalry regiments under the emperor's direct command, grant them arms and supplies superior to other armies, appoint Chengyou as overall commander of Dragon Martial infantry and cavalry, with the lieutenant general An Chongba as deputy—all the veteran generals were indignant and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengyou, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Shu Palace Secretariat, asked to pick twelve thousand of the boldest troops from every army and form forty Left and Right Dragon Martial infantry and cavalry regiments under the ruler's direct command, with arms and pay better than any other unit. Chengyou was made overall commander of the Dragon Martial Army, with the lieutenant general An Chongba as his deputy—and every veteran general seethed with anger and shame.

sentences.zh: 重霸，去州人，以狡佞賄賂事承休，故承休悅之。

translations.literal: Chongba was a native of Quzhou; through cunning flattery and bribes he served Chengyou, which was why Chengyou favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongba was from Quzhou and had won Chengyou's favor through sly flattery and bribery.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐復修本朝職貢，壬午，帝因梁官爵而命之。

translations.literal: The King of Wuyue, Qian Liu, renewed tribute and duties to our court; on the renwu day, the emperor appointed him using Liang titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wuyue, Qian Liu, restored tribute and formal duties to the Later Tang court; on the renwu day the emperor confirmed his appointment using the titles and ranks of the Liang regime.

sentences.zh: 鏐厚貢獻，並賂權要，求金印、玉冊、賜詔不名、稱國王。

translations.literal: Qian made lavish tribute and bribed influential officials, requesting a gold seal, jade investiture book, an edict that did not use his personal name, and the title of king of a state.
translations.idiomatic: Qian sent lavish tribute and bribed powerful officials, asking for a gold seal, a jade investiture book, an edict that omitted his personal name, and the title of king of a state.

sentences.zh: 有司言：「故事惟天子用玉冊，王公皆用竹冊；

translations.literal: The responsible officials said: "By precedent, only the Son of Heaven used jade investiture books; princes and dukes all used bamboo books;
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices objected: "By precedent only the Son of Heaven received a jade investiture book; princes and dukes used bamboo books;

sentences.zh: 又，非四夷無封國王者。」

translations.literal: moreover, only foreign peoples received kings over designated states."
translations.idiomatic: moreover, only foreign peoples were enfeoffed as kings over designated states."

sentences.zh: 帝皆曲從鏐意。

translations.literal: The emperor acceded to Qian's wishes in every case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bent precedent in every case to satisfy Qian.

sentences.zh: 吳王如白沙觀樓船，更命白沙曰迎鑾鎮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wu went to Baisha to inspect the tower ships and renamed Baisha to Yingluan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wu went to Baisha to review the tower ships and renamed the place Yingluan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徐溫自金陵來朝，先是，溫以親吏翟虔為閣門、宮城、武備等使，使察王起居，虔防制王甚急。

translations.literal: Xu Wen came to court from Jinling; earlier, Wen had placed his close aide Zhai Qian as commissioner for palace gates, the palace city, military stores, and other matters to observe the prince's daily activities—Qian's restrictions on the prince were extremely tight.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen came to court from Jinling. Earlier he had placed his trusted aide Zhai Qian in charge of palace gates, the palace city, military stores, and related duties to watch the prince's every move—and Qian's control over the prince had been suffocatingly tight.

sentences.zh: 至是，王對溫名雨為水，溫請其故。

translations.literal: At this point, when speaking to Wen the prince called rain "water"; Wen asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, when speaking with Wen the prince called rain "water," and Wen asked why.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「翟虔父名，吾諱之熟矣。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "Qian's father's given name—I am thoroughly practiced in avoiding it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "Qian's father's given name—I have grown very practiced at avoiding it.

sentences.zh: 因謂溫曰：「公之忠誠，我所知也，然翟虔無禮，宮中及宗室所須多不獲。」

translations.literal: Then he told Wen: "Your loyalty I know well, but Zhai Qian is insolent—the palace and the imperial clan often cannot obtain what they need.
translations.idiomatic: Then he added: "Your loyalty I know well, but Zhai Qian is insolent—the palace and the imperial clan often cannot get what they need.

sentences.zh: 溫頓首謝罪，請斬之，王曰：「斬則太過，遠徙可也。」

translations.literal: Wen kowtowed and apologized, asking to have him executed; the prince said: "Execution would be excessive—a distant transfer will do.
translations.idiomatic: Wen kowtowed and apologized, asking to have Qian executed. The prince said: "Execution would be too much—a distant transfer will do.

sentences.zh: 乃徙撫州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，蜀主遣其翰林學士歐陽彬來聘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Shu ruler sent his Hanlin academician Ouyang Bin on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the Shu ruler sent his Hanlin academician Ouyang Bin on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 彬，衡山人也。

translations.literal: Bin was a native of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was a native of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 又遣李彥稠東還。

translations.literal: He also sent Li Yanchou back east.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Li Yanchou back to the east.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝帥親軍獵於伊闕，命從官拜梁太祖墓。

translations.literal: On the guimao day, the emperor led the imperial guard on a hunt at Yique and ordered his attendants to bow before the tomb of the Liang founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, the emperor led the imperial guard on a hunt at Yique and ordered his attendants to pay respects at the tomb of the Liang founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 涉歷山險，連日不止，或夜合圍；

translations.literal: They traversed perilous mountains, hunting for days without stopping, sometimes encircling game by night;
translations.idiomatic: They crossed treacherous mountain country and hunted for days without pause, sometimes driving the beat at night;

sentences.zh: 士卒墜崖谷死及折傷者甚眾。

translations.literal: many soldiers died falling from cliffs and ravines or were badly injured.
translations.idiomatic: many soldiers died falling into ravines or were badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 丙午，還宮。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 蜀以唐修好，罷威武城戍，召關宏業等二十四軍還成都。

translations.literal: Because Shu had made peace with Tang, it abolished the garrison at Weiwu Fort and recalled the twenty-four armies of Guan Hongye and others to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shu had made peace with Tang, it withdrew the garrison at Weiwu Fort and recalled the twenty-four armies under Guan Hongye and others to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 戊申，又罷武定、武興招討劉潛等三十七軍。

translations.literal: On the wushen day, it also abolished the suppression commands for Wuding and Wuxing and recalled the thirty-seven armies of Liu Qian and others.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, it also dissolved the Wuding and Wuxing suppression commands and recalled the thirty-seven armies under Liu Qian and others.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，賜護國節度使李繼麟鐵券，以其子令德、令錫皆為節度使，諸子勝衣者即拜官，寵冠列籓。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day, Li Jilin, military governor of Huguo, was granted an iron certificate of immunity; both his sons Lingde and Lingxi were made military governors, and any son old enough to wear adult robes was immediately given an office—his favor surpassed all other regional lords.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day, Li Jilin, military governor of Huguo, received an iron certificate of immunity; both his sons Lingde and Lingxi were made military governors, and every son old enough to wear adult robes was immediately given an office—no regional lord enjoyed greater favor.

sentences.zh: 庚申，蔚州言契丹入寇。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day, Weizhou reported that the Khitan had invaded.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day, Weizhou reported a Khitan incursion.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，蜀主罷天雄軍招討，命王承騫等二十九軍還成都。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day, the Shu ruler abolished the Tianxiong Army suppression command and ordered the twenty-nine armies of Wang Chengqian and others to return to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day, the Shu ruler dissolved the Tianxiong Army suppression command and ordered the twenty-nine armies under Wang Chengqian and others back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙丑朔，蜀主以右僕射張格兼中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the yichou day, the first of the month, the Shu ruler made Right Deputy Director Zhang Ge concurrently Secretariat Vice Director and co-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the yichou day, the first of the month, the Shu ruler made Right Deputy Director Zhang Ge concurrently Secretariat Vice Director and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 初，格之得罪，中書吏王魯柔乘危窘之；
