translations.literal: When Zhang had first fallen from favor, the Secretariat clerk Wang Rourou had seized the crisis to hound him;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang had first fallen from power, the Secretariat clerk Wang Rourou had seized the moment to humiliate him;

sentences.zh: 及再為相用事，杖殺之。

translations.literal: when he again became chief minister and wielded power, he had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhang returned to office and took power, he had Rourou beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 許寂謂人曰：「張公才高而識淺，戮一魯柔，他人誰敢自保！

translations.literal: Xu Ji told others: "Lord Zhang's talent is high but his judgment shallow—when he kills one Rourou, who else will dare feel safe!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji remarked to others: "Lord Zhang's talent is great but his judgment shallow—kill one Rourou, and who else will dare feel safe!

sentences.zh: 此取禍之端也。」

translations.literal: This is the beginning of inviting disaster."
translations.idiomatic: This is the start of inviting disaster."

sentences.zh: 蜀主罷金州屯戍，命王承勳等七軍還成都。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler abolished the garrison at Jinzhou and ordered the seven armies of Wang Chengxun and others back to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler withdrew the Jinzhou garrison and ordered the seven armies under Wang Chengxun and others back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 己巳，命宣武節度使李嗣源將宿衛兵三萬七千人赴汴州，遂如幽州御契丹。

translations.literal: On the jisi day, Li Siyuan, military governor of Xuanwu, was ordered to lead thirty-seven thousand palace guard troops to Bianzhou, then proceed to Youzhou to repel the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, Li Siyuan, military governor of Xuanwu, was ordered to lead thirty-seven thousand palace guard troops to Bianzhou and then on to Youzhou to repel the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝及皇后如張全義第，全義大陳貢獻；

translations.literal: On the gengwu day, the emperor and the empress visited Zhang Quanyi's residence; Quanyi laid out lavish tribute offerings;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day, the emperor and empress visited Zhang Quanyi's residence, where Quanyi laid out lavish tribute;

sentences.zh: 酒酣，皇后奏稱：「妾幼失父母，見老者輒思之，請父事全義。」

translations.literal: When the wine had warmed them, the empress said: "I lost my parents young—whenever I see an elder I think of them; I ask to treat Quanyi as a father.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had warmed them, the empress said: "I lost my parents young—whenever I see an elder I miss them; I ask to treat Quanyi as a father.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 全義惶恐固辭，再三強之，竟受皇后拜，復貢獻謝恩。

translations.literal: Quanyi, terrified, firmly refused, but after repeated insistence he ultimately accepted the empress's bow and again presented tribute to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi, terrified, refused again and again, but after repeated insistence he finally accepted the empress's bow and again sent tribute to express his thanks.

sentences.zh: 明日，後命翰林學士趙鳳草書謝全義，鳳密奏：「自古無天下之母拜人臣為父者。」

translations.literal: The next day the empress ordered Hanlin academician Zhao Feng to draft a letter of thanks to Quanyi; Feng secretly memorialized: "Since antiquity there has never been a Mother of the Realm bowing to a subject as father.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the empress ordered Hanlin academician Zhao Feng to draft a letter of thanks to Quanyi. Feng secretly memorialized: "Since antiquity there has never been a Mother of the Realm bowing to a subject as father.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其直，然卒行之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his frankness yet carried it through anyway.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his frankness but carried the arrangement through anyway.

sentences.zh: 自是後與全義日遣使往來問遺不絕。

translations.literal: From then on the emperor and Quanyi sent envoys back and forth daily with gifts without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor and Quanyi exchanged envoys and gifts every day without pause.

sentences.zh: 初，唐僖、昭之世，宦官雖盛，未嘗有建節者。

translations.literal: In the eras of Emperors Xizong and Zhaozong of Tang, although eunuchs were powerful, none had ever been granted a military commission with the ceremonial axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the reigns of Tang Emperors Xizong and Zhaozong, eunuchs had been powerful, yet none had ever been granted a military commission with the ceremonial axe.

sentences.zh: 蜀安重霸勸王承休求秦州節度使，承休言於蜀主曰：「秦州多美婦人，請為陛下采擇以獻。」

translations.literal: Shu's An Chongba urged Wang Chengyou to seek appointment as military governor of Qinzhou; Chengyou said to the Shu ruler: "Qinzhou has many beautiful women—I ask to select some to present to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, An Chongba urged Wang Chengyou to seek appointment as military governor of Qinzhou. Chengyou told the Shu ruler: "Qinzhou has many beautiful women—I ask to choose some to present to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 蜀主許之，庚午，以承休為天雄節度使，封魯國公；

translations.literal: The Shu ruler granted it; on the gengwu day Chengyou was made military governor of Tianxiong and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu;
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler agreed. On the gengwu day Chengyou was made military governor of Tianxiong and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu;

sentences.zh: 以龍武軍為承休牙兵。

translations.literal: the Dragon Martial Army was made Chengyou's personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: and the Dragon Martial Army was assigned as Chengyou's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，蜀主以前武德節度使兼中書令徐延瓊為京城內外馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: On the yihai day, the Shu ruler appointed former Wude military governor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat Xu Yanqiong as overall commander of capital infantry and cavalry, inside and outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day, the Shu ruler appointed former Wude military governor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat Xu Yanqiong overall commander of capital infantry and cavalry, inside and outside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 延瓊以外戚代王宗弼居舊將之右，眾皆不平。

translations.literal: As a maternal relative Yanqiong replaced Wang Zongbi in rank above the veteran generals—all were resentful.
translations.idiomatic: As a maternal kinsman Yanqiong took Wang Zongbi's place above the veteran generals, and everyone resented it.

sentences.zh: 壬午，北京言契丹寇嵐州。

translations.literal: On the renwu day, the Northern Capital reported that the Khitan had raided Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day, the Northern Capital reported that the Khitan had raided Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，蜀主改明年元曰咸康。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day, the Shu ruler changed the next year's era name to Xiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day, the Shu ruler changed the next year's era name to Xiankang.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使李存賢卒。

translations.literal: Li Cunxian, military governor of Lulong, died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxian, military governor of Lulong, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蜀主徙普王宗仁為衛王。

translations.literal: That year the Shu ruler changed Prince Pu Zongren to Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Shu ruler changed Prince Pu Zongren's title to Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 雅王宗輅為幽王，褒王宗紀為趙王，榮王宗智為韓王，興王宗澤為宋王，彭王宗鼎為魯王，忠王宗平為薛王，資王宗特為莒王；

translations.literal: Prince Ya Zongluo became Prince of You, Prince Bao Zongji became Prince of Zhao, Prince Rong Zongzhi became Prince of Han, Prince Xing Zongze became Prince of Song, Prince Peng Zongding became Prince of Lu, Prince Zhong Zongping became Prince of Xue, and Prince Zi Zongte became Prince of Ju;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ya Zongluo became Prince of You, Prince Bao Zongji Prince of Zhao, Prince Rong Zongzhi Prince of Han, Prince Xing Zongze Prince of Song, Prince Peng Zongding Prince of Lu, Prince Zhong Zongping Prince of Xue, and Prince Zi Zongte Prince of Ju;

sentences.zh: 宗輅、宗智、宗平皆罷軍使。

translations.literal: Zongluo, Zongzhi, and Zongping were all removed from military command.
translations.idiomatic: Zongluo, Zongzhi, and Zongping were all stripped of their military commands.

sentences.zh: 莊宗光聖神閔孝皇帝中同光三年（

translations.literal: Middle reign of Emperor Zhuangzong Guangchengshenminxiao, third year of Tongguang (
translations.idiomatic: Middle reign of Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang, third year of Tongguang (

sentences.zh: 乙酉，公元九二五年）

translations.literal: yiyou, corresponding to the year 925 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: yiyou, AD 925)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲午朔，蜀大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jiawu day, the first of the month, Shu declared a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the jiawu day, the first of the month, Shu declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙申，敕有司改葬昭宗及少帝，竟以用度不足而止。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day, an edict ordered the responsible offices to rebury Emperor Zhaozong and the Young Emperor, but it was ultimately halted for insufficient funds.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day, an edict ordered the responsible offices to rebury Emperor Zhaozong and the Young Emperor, but the project was abandoned for lack of funds.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇幽州。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan raided Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，帝發洛陽；

translations.literal: On the gengzi day, the emperor departed Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day, the emperor left Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 庚戌，至興唐。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day, he reached Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, he reached Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 詔平盧節度使苻習治酸棗遙堤以御決河。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Fu Xi, military governor of Pinglu, to repair the Suanzao distant levee to guard against a breached Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Fu Xi, military governor of Pinglu, to repair the Suanzao distant levee to guard against a breach of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 初，李嗣源北征，過興唐，東京庫有供御細鎧，嗣源牒副留守張憲取五百領，憲以軍興，不暇奏而給之；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Siyuan marched north, passing Xingtang, the Eastern Capital storehouse held fine armor for imperial use; Siyuan sent a dispatch to deputy prefect Zhang Xian to take five hundred sets—Xian, with troops mobilized, had no time to memorialize and supplied them;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Li Siyuan marched north and passed through Xingtang, the Eastern Capital storehouse held fine armor reserved for imperial use. Siyuan sent a dispatch to deputy prefect Zhang Xian requesting five hundred sets; with troops mobilized, Xian had no time to memorialize and issued them;

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「憲不奉詔，擅以吾鎧給嗣源，何意也！」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Xian did not await imperial command yet presumptuously gave my armor to Siyuan—what did he mean by this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said: "Xian did not await imperial command yet gave my armor to Siyuan on his own authority—what did he mean by that!

sentences.zh: 罰憲俸一月，令自往軍中取之。

translations.literal: He fined Xian one month's salary and ordered him to go to the army camp in person to retrieve the armor.
translations.idiomatic: He fined Xian one month's salary and ordered him to go to the army camp in person to recover the armor.

sentences.zh: 帝以義武節度使王都將入朝，欲辟球場，憲曰：「此以行宮闕廷為球場，前年陛下即位於此。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Wang Du, military governor of Yiwu, was coming to court, wished to clear a polo ground; Xian said: "This would make the provisional palace court into a polo ground—the year before last Your Majesty took the throne here.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wang Du, military governor of Yiwu, was coming to court, the emperor wanted to clear a polo ground. Xian said: "That would turn the provisional palace court into a polo ground—the year before last Your Majesty took the throne here.

sentences.zh: 其壇不可毀，請辟球場於宮西。」

translations.literal: That altar must not be destroyed; I ask that the polo ground be cleared west of the palace."
translations.idiomatic: That altar must not be destroyed. I ask that the polo ground be cleared west of the palace."

sentences.zh: 數日，未成，帝命毀即位壇。

translations.literal: Several days passed without completion, and the emperor ordered the enthronement altar destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Several days passed without the new ground being ready, and the emperor ordered the enthronement altar torn down.

sentences.zh: 憲謂郭崇韜曰：「此壇，主上所以禮上帝，始受命之地也，若之何毀之！」

translations.literal: Xian said to Guo Chongtao: "This altar is where His Majesty worshipped Heaven—the place where he first received the Mandate; how can it be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: Xian told Guo Chongtao: "This altar is where His Majesty worshipped Heaven—the place where he first received the Mandate. How can it be destroyed!

sentences.zh: 崇韜從容言於帝，帝立命兩虞候毀之。

translations.literal: Chongtao spoke calmly to the emperor, but the emperor immediately ordered two palace guards to destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao spoke to the emperor in a measured tone, but the emperor immediately ordered two palace guards to destroy it.

sentences.zh: 憲私於崇韜曰：「忘天背本，不祥莫大焉。」

translations.literal: Xian privately told Chongtao: "To forget Heaven and turn one's back on one's origins—nothing could be more ill-omened."
translations.idiomatic: Xian privately told Chongtao: "To forget Heaven and turn one's back on one's origins—nothing could be more ill-omened."

sentences.zh: 二月，甲戌，以橫海節度使李紹斌為盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the jiaxu day, Li Shaobin, military governor of Henghai, was made military governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the jiaxu day, Li Shaobin, military governor of Henghai, was appointed military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 丙子，李嗣源奏敗契丹於涿州。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day, Li Siyuan memorialized that he had defeated the Khitan at Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day, Li Siyuan reported that he had defeated the Khitan at Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 上以契丹為憂，與郭崇韜謀，以威名宿將零落殆盡，李紹斌位望素輕，欲徙李嗣源鎮真定，為紹斌聲援，崇韜深以為便。

translations.literal: The emperor, anxious about the Khitan, consulted with Guo Chongtao; since famed veteran generals had nearly all died off and Li Shaobin's standing was inherently slight, he wished to transfer Li Siyuan to defend Zhending as reinforcement for Shaobin—Chongtao strongly favored the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious about the Khitan, the emperor consulted Guo Chongtao. With famed veteran generals nearly all gone and Li Shaobin's standing inherently slight, he wanted to transfer Li Siyuan to Zhending to reinforce Shaobin—and Chongtao strongly approved.

sentences.zh: 時崇韜領真定，上欲徙崇韜鎮汴州，崇韜辭曰：「臣內典樞機，外預大政，富貴極矣，何必更領籓方？

translations.literal: At the time Chongtao held Zhending; the emperor wished to transfer Chongtao to govern Bianzhou; Chongtao declined: "Within I manage the key mechanisms, without I share in great affairs—my wealth and rank are at their height; why must I govern a frontier circuit as well?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chongtao held Zhending, and the emperor wanted to transfer him to Bianzhou. Chongtao declined: "Within I manage the key mechanisms of state, without I share in great affairs—my wealth and rank are already at their height. Why must I govern a frontier circuit as well?

sentences.zh: 且群臣或從陛下歲久，身經百戰，所得不過一州。

translations.literal: Moreover, many ministers have followed Your Majesty for years, fought a hundred battles, and gained no more than a single prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Many of your ministers have followed Your Majesty for years, fought a hundred battles, and received no more than a single prefecture.

sentences.zh: 臣無汗馬之勞，徒以侍從左右，時贊聖謨，致位至此，常不自安；

translations.literal: I have no sweat-of-the-horse merit—I rose to this place merely by attending at Your Majesty's side and occasionally advising on policy, and I am never at ease;
translations.idiomatic: I have no sweat-of-the-horse merit. I rose to this place merely by attending at Your Majesty's side and occasionally advising on policy, and I am never at ease;

sentences.zh: 今因委任勳賢，使臣得解旄節，乃大願也。

translations.literal: Now, by entrusting meritorious worthies, if I am allowed to surrender my command banner and axe, that would be my greatest wish.
translations.idiomatic: Now, by entrusting meritorious men, if I am allowed to surrender my command banner and axe, that would be my greatest wish.

sentences.zh: 且汴州關東衝要，地富人繁，臣既不至治所，徒令他人攝職，何異空城！

translations.literal: Moreover Bianzhou is the critical gate of the east, rich land with a dense population—if I never go to my post yet leave others to act in my stead, how is that different from an empty city!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Bianzhou is the critical gateway of the east, rich and densely populated—if I never go to my post and leave others to act in my stead, how is that different from holding an empty city!

sentences.zh: 非所以固國基也。」

translations.literal: It is no way to secure the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: That is no way to secure the foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「深知卿忠盡，然卿為朕畫策，襲取汶陽，保固河津，既而自此路乘虛直趨大梁，成朕帝業，豈百戰之功可比乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I know well your loyalty, yet you devised the plan to seize Wenyang, secure the Yellow River crossings, and then drive straight for Daliang along that route while the enemy was exposed—thus completing my imperial enterprise; how can that compare to merit won in a hundred battles!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I know your loyalty well, yet you devised the plan to seize Wenyang, secure the Yellow River crossings, and then drive straight for Daliang along that route while the enemy was exposed—thus completing my imperial enterprise. How can that compare to merit won in a hundred battles!

sentences.zh: 今朕貴為天子，豈可使卿曾無尺寸之地乎！」

translations.literal: Now that I am exalted as Son of Heaven, how can I let you have not even an inch of territory!
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am exalted as Son of Heaven, how can I let you hold not even an inch of territory!

sentences.zh: 崇韜固辭不已，上乃許之。

translations.literal: Chongtao continued to refuse firmly, and the emperor finally agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao kept refusing, and the emperor finally relented.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，徙李嗣源為成德節度使。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day Li Siyuan was transferred to be military governor of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day Li Siyuan was transferred to military governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 漢主聞帝滅梁而懼，遣宮苑使何詞入貢，且覘中國強弱。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han, hearing that the emperor had destroyed Liang, was afraid and sent Palace Gardens Commissioner He Ci to present tribute and also to spy out the strength or weakness of the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han, hearing that the emperor had destroyed Liang, was afraid and sent Palace Gardens Commissioner He Ci to present tribute and also to gauge the strength of the Central Realm.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詞至魏。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day Ci reached Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day He Ci reached Wei.

sentences.zh: 及還，言帝驕淫無政，不足畏也。

translations.literal: When he returned he reported that the emperor was arrogant, licentious, and neglectful of government—not worth fearing.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he reported that the emperor was arrogant, licentious, and neglectful of government—not worth fearing.

sentences.zh: 漢主大悅，自是不復通中國。

translations.literal: The Han ruler was greatly pleased and from then on no longer maintained contact with the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler was greatly pleased and from then on ceased all contact with the Central Realm.

sentences.zh: 帝性剛好勝，不欲權在臣下，入洛之後，信伶宦之讒，頗疏忌宿將。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature stubborn and competitive, unwilling to let power rest with his ministers; after entering Luoyang he believed slander from actors and eunuchs and grew quite distant and suspicious toward veteran generals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was by nature stubborn and competitive and unwilling to let power rest with his ministers. After entering Luoyang he believed slander from actors and eunuchs and grew distant and suspicious toward veteran generals.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源家在太原，三月，丁酉，表衛州刺史李從珂為北京內牙馬步都指揮使以便其家，帝怒曰：「嗣源握兵權，居大鎮，軍政在吾，安得為其子奏請！」

translations.literal: Li Siyuan's family was in Taiyuan; in the third month, on the dingyou day, he memorialized to appoint Li Congke, prefect of Weizhou, as commander of the inner cavalry and infantry of the Northern Capital to accommodate his family; the emperor angrily said: "Siyuan holds military power and governs a great circuit—military affairs are mine; how dare he memorialize on behalf of his son!
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan's family was in Taiyuan. In the third month, on the dingyou day, he memorialized to appoint Li Congke, prefect of Weizhou, as commander of the inner cavalry and infantry of the Northern Capital to accommodate his family. The emperor angrily said: "Siyuan holds military power and governs a great circuit—military affairs are mine. How dare he memorialize on behalf of his son!

sentences.zh: 乃黜從珂為突騎指揮使，帥數百人戍石門鎮。

translations.literal: Li Congke was demoted to commander of the Tiger Cavalry and led several hundred men to garrison Shimen Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congke was demoted to commander of the Tiger Cavalry and led several hundred men to garrison Shimen Fort.

sentences.zh: 嗣源憂恐，上章申理，久之方解。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan was anxious and fearful; he submitted a memorial pleading his case, and only after a long time was the matter resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan lived in anxiety and dread, memorializing the throne to clear his name; only after a long while was the affair laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，嗣源乞至東京朝覲，不許。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Li Siyuan petitioned to come to the Eastern Capital for an audience; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Li Siyuan asked leave to come to the Eastern Capital for an audience; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜以嗣源功高位重，亦忌之，私謂人曰：「總管令公非久為人下者，皇家子弟皆不及也。」

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao, seeing Li Siyuan's high merit and lofty rank, also envied him; in private he told others, "The Overall Commander and Duke is not one who will long remain beneath others—all the imperial princes fall short of him."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao, seeing Li Siyuan's towering merit and rank, envied him as well; in private he told others, "The Overall Commander and Duke is not a man who will long serve beneath another—the imperial princes are none of them his equal."

sentences.zh: 密勸帝召之宿衛，罷其兵權，又勸帝除之，帝皆不從。

translations.literal: He secretly urged the emperor to summon Li Siyuan to serve as palace guard, strip him of military authority, and even urged the emperor to eliminate him—but the emperor would not heed any of it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly urged the emperor to summon Li Siyuan to palace guard duty, strip him of command, and even to eliminate him—but the emperor would not listen to any of it.

sentences.zh: 己酉，帝發興唐，自德勝濟河，歷楊村、戚城，觀昔時戰處，指示群臣以為樂。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the emperor set out from Xingtang; crossing the Yellow River from Desheng, he passed Yang Village and Qicheng, viewing the old battlegrounds and pointing them out to his ministers for their amusement.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the emperor departed Xingtang, crossed the Yellow River at Desheng, and passed through Yang Village and Qicheng, touring the old battlefields and showing them to his ministers for sport.

sentences.zh: 洛陽宮殿宏邃，宦者欲上增廣嬪御，詐言宮中夜見鬼物。

translations.literal: The Luoyang palace was vast and deep; eunuchs wished the emperor to expand the consort quarters and falsely claimed that ghostly apparitions were seen in the palace at night.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyang palace was vast and deep; the eunuchs wanted the emperor to enlarge the consort quarters and falsely claimed that spirits walked the halls at night.

sentences.zh: 上欲使符咒者攘之，宦者曰：「臣昔逮事咸通、乾符天子，當是時，六宮貴賤不減萬人。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to have exorcists drive them away; a eunuch said, "Your servant once served the emperors of the Xiantong and Qianfu reigns—in those days the inner palaces counted no fewer than ten thousand women of every rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to send in exorcists when a eunuch said, "Your servant once served the Xiantong and Qianfu emperors—in those days the inner palaces held no fewer than ten thousand women, high and low.

sentences.zh: 今掖庭太半空虛，故鬼物游之耳。」

translations.literal: Now the rear palace is more than half empty, so ghostly beings roam it."
translations.idiomatic: Now the rear palace stands more than half empty—that is why spirits roam it."

sentences.zh: 上乃命宦者王允平、伶人景進采擇民間女子，遠至太原、幽、鎮，以充後庭，不啻三千人，不問所從來。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the eunuch Wang Yunping and the actor Jing Jin to gather common women from as far as Taiyuan, You, and Zhen to fill the rear palace—no fewer than three thousand, with no inquiry into where they came from.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the eunuch Wang Yunping and the actor Jing Jin to gather common women from as far as Taiyuan, You, and Zhen to fill the rear palace—no fewer than three thousand, without asking whence they came.

sentences.zh: 上還自興唐，載以牛車，纍纍盈路。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Xingtang, they were transported in ox carts, filling the roads in endless lines.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Xingtang, the women rode in ox carts that filled the roads in endless lines.

sentences.zh: 張憲奏：「諸營婦女亡逸者千餘人，慮扈從諸軍挾匿以行。」

translations.literal: Zhang Xian reported: "Over a thousand camp women have fled; I fear the accompanying armies are secreting them along the route."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian reported, "More than a thousand camp women have vanished; I fear the armies on the march are hiding them among the ranks."

sentences.zh: 其實皆入宮矣。

translations.literal: In truth they had all entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In truth they had all been taken into the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝至洛陽；

translations.literal: On gengchen, the emperor arrived at Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor reached Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔復以洛陽為東都，興唐府為鄴都。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict restored Luoyang as the Eastern Capital and Xingtang Prefecture as the Ye Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou an edict restored Luoyang as the Eastern Capital and Xingtang Prefecture as the Ye Capital.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the guihai new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the guihai new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 初，五台僧誠惠以妖妄惑人，自言能降伏天龍，命風召雨；

translations.literal: Initially, the Wutai monk Chenghui deluded people with sorcery, claiming he could subdue heavenly dragons and command wind and summon rain;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Wutai monk Chenghui had beguiled the people with sorcery, claiming he could subdue heavenly dragons and command wind and rain;

sentences.zh: 帝尊信之，親帥后妃及皇弟、皇子拜之，誠惠安坐不起，群臣莫敢不拜，獨郭崇韜不拜。

translations.literal: The emperor revered and trusted him, personally leading consorts, imperial brothers, and princes to pay obeisance; Chenghui sat undisturbed and did not rise—none among the ministers dared not bow save Guo Chongtao alone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revered and trusted him, personally leading consorts, imperial brothers, and princes to bow before him; Chenghui sat at ease and did not rise—every minister bowed save Guo Chongtao alone.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，帝自鄴都迎誠惠至洛陽，使祈雨，士民朝夕瞻仰，數旬不雨。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought; the emperor brought Chenghui from the Ye Capital to Luoyang and had him pray for rain—the people looked up to him morning and evening, yet for many weeks no rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: There was a great drought; the emperor brought Chenghui from the Ye Capital to Luoyang to pray for rain, and the people looked to him morning and night—yet for many weeks no rain came.

sentences.zh: 或謂誠惠：「官以師祈雨無驗，將焚之。」

translations.literal: Someone told Chenghui, "The authorities, finding your rain prayers unavailing, will burn you."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Chenghui, "The authorities say your prayers brought no rain—they mean to burn you."

sentences.zh: 誠惠逃去，慚懼而卒。

translations.literal: Chenghui fled; shamed and afraid, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui fled; shamed and terrified, he died.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，中書侍郎、同平章事趙光胤卒。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-equal Assessor Zhao Guangyin died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-equal Assessor Zhao Guangyin died.

sentences.zh: 太后自與太妃別，常忽忽不樂，雖娛玩盈前，未嘗解顏；

translations.literal: Since parting from the Grand Consort, the empress dowager had often been listless and unhappy; though diversions crowded before her, she never softened her countenance;
translations.idiomatic: Since parting from the Grand Consort, the empress dowager had been listless and unhappy; though diversions crowded before her, she never once softened her face;

sentences.zh: 太妃既別太后，亦邑邑成疾。

translations.literal: After parting from the empress dowager, the Grand Consort too fell ill with melancholy.
translations.idiomatic: After parting from the empress dowager, the Grand Consort too fell ill with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 太后遣中使醫藥相繼於道，聞疾稍加，輒不食，又謂帝曰：「吾與太妃恩如兄弟，欲自往省之。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager sent palace emissaries with physicians and medicines in endless succession; learning her illness had slightly improved, she would at once refuse food, and told the emperor, "The Grand Consort and I are bound like sisters—I wish to go myself to visit her."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent palace emissaries with physicians and medicines in an unbroken stream; when she heard the Grand Consort's illness had eased a little, she would at once refuse food, and told the emperor, "The Grand Consort and I are bound like sisters—I wish to go and see her myself."

sentences.zh: 帝以天暑道遠，苦諫，久之乃止，但遣皇弟存渥等往迎侍。

translations.literal: The emperor, citing the heat of summer and the distance of the road, pleaded earnestly against it; after long persuasion she stopped, and he sent only the imperial brother Cunwo and others to fetch and attend her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, citing the summer heat and the long road, pleaded hard against it; after long persuasion she relented, and he sent only the imperial brother Cunwo and others to fetch and attend her.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁酉，北都奏太妃薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingyou, the Northern Capital reported the Grand Consort had died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingyou, the Northern Capital reported that the Grand Consort had died.

sentences.zh: 太后悲哀不食者累日，帝寬譬不離左右。

translations.literal: The empress dowager mourned and would not eat for many days; the emperor comforted her and would not leave her side.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager grieved and would not eat for many days; the emperor comforted her and would not leave her side.

sentences.zh: 太后自是得疾，又欲自往會太妃葬，帝力諫而止。

translations.literal: Thereafter the empress dowager fell ill herself, and again wished to go in person to the Grand Consort's funeral; the emperor pleaded forcefully and stopped her.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the empress dowager fell ill herself and again wished to attend the Grand Consort's funeral in person; the emperor pleaded forcefully and stopped her.

sentences.zh: 閩王審知寢疾，命其子節度副使延翰權知軍府事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Min, Shenzhi, lay ill in bed and ordered his son, deputy military governor Yanhan, to provisionally manage headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Min, Shenzhi, lay gravely ill and ordered his son, deputy military governor Yanhan, to provisionally manage headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 自春夏大旱，六月，壬申，始雨。

translations.literal: Since spring and summer had brought great drought, in the sixth month, on renshen, rain at last began.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and summer had brought great drought; in the sixth month, on renshen, rain at last began.

sentences.zh: 帝苦溽暑，於禁中擇高涼之所，皆不稱旨。

translations.literal: The emperor suffered from the sweltering heat; within the forbidden precincts he chose every high and cool place, yet none pleased him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suffered from the sweltering heat; within the forbidden precincts he tried every high and cool spot, yet none pleased him.

sentences.zh: 宦者因言：「臣見長安全盛時，大明、興慶宮樓觀以百數。

translations.literal: A eunuch then spoke: "Your servant saw Chang'an in its full splendor—the Daming and Xingqing palaces had towers and pavilions numbering in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch then spoke: "Your servant saw Chang'an in its full splendor—the Daming and Xingqing palaces had towers and pavilions by the hundred.

sentences.zh: 今日宅家曾無避暑之所，宮殿之盛曾不及當時公卿第捨耳。」

translations.literal: Today His Majesty has no place to escape the heat; the grandeur of the palace does not even match the mansions of the great ministers of that time."
translations.idiomatic: Today His Majesty has nowhere to escape the heat; the palace is not even as grand as the mansions of the great ministers of that day."

sentences.zh: 帝乃命宮苑使王允平別建一樓以清暑。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the palace parks commissioner Wang Yunping to build a separate tower for clearing away the heat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the palace parks commissioner Wang Yunping to build a separate tower to escape the heat.

sentences.zh: 宦者曰：「郭崇韜常不伸眉，為孔謙論用度不足，恐陛下雖欲營繕，終不可得。」

translations.literal: A eunuch said, "Guo Chongtao is ever frowning, arguing with Kong Qian over insufficient funds—I'm afraid even if Your Majesty wishes to build, you will never obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch said, "Guo Chongtao is ever frowning, quarreling with Kong Qian over insufficient funds—I fear that even if Your Majesty wishes to build, you will never get your way."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾自用內府錢，無關經費。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I shall use the inner treasury's funds—it has nothing to do with state expenses."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I shall use the inner treasury's funds—it has nothing to do with state expenses."

sentences.zh: 然猶慮崇韜諫，遣中使語之曰：「今歲盛暑異常，朕昔在河上，與梁人相拒，行營卑濕，被甲乘馬，親當矢石，猶無此暑。

translations.literal: Yet he still feared Chongtao would remonstrate, and sent a palace emissary to tell him, "This year's heat is extraordinary. When I was on the Yellow River facing the Liang forces, the camps were low and damp; clad in armor and mounted, I faced arrows and stones myself—yet even then the heat was not like this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still feared Chongtao would remonstrate, and sent a palace emissary to tell him, "This year's heat is extraordinary. When I was on the Yellow River facing the Liang, the camps were low and damp; clad in armor and mounted, I faced arrows and stones myself—yet even then the heat was not like this.

sentences.zh: 今居深宮之中而暑不可度，奈何？」

translations.literal: Now dwelling deep within the palace I cannot endure the heat—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now dwelling deep within the palace I cannot endure the heat—what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下昔在河上，勍敵未滅，深念仇恥，雖有盛暑，不介聖懷。

translations.literal: Chongtao replied, "When Your Majesty was on the river, fierce enemies were not yet destroyed; you brooded deeply on enmity and shame—though the heat was fierce, it did not touch your sacred mind.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao replied, "When Your Majesty was on the river, fierce enemies were not yet destroyed; you brooded on enmity and shame—though the heat was fierce, it did not touch your mind.

sentences.zh: 今外患已除，海內賓服，故雖珍台閒館猶覺郁蒸也。

translations.literal: Now external threats are gone and the realm submits; thus even within jeweled towers and idle halls you feel the stifling air.
translations.idiomatic: Now external threats are gone and the realm submits; thus even within jeweled towers and idle halls you feel the stifling air.

sentences.zh: 陛下倘不忘艱難之時，則暑氣自消矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would but remember the hard years, the heat would vanish of itself."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would but remember the hard years, the heat would vanish of itself."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 宦者曰：「崇韜之第，無異皇居，宜其不知至尊之熱也。」

translations.literal: A eunuch said, "Chongtao's mansion is no different from the imperial residence—no wonder he cannot grasp how hot the Son of Heaven is."
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch said, "Chongtao's mansion is no different from the imperial residence—no wonder he cannot grasp how hot the Son of Heaven is."

sentences.zh: 帝卒命允平營樓，日役萬人，所費巨萬。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately ordered Yunping to build the tower; ten thousand men labored daily, at cost in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately ordered Yunping to build the tower; ten thousand men labored each day, at a cost in the tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 崇韜諫曰：「今兩河水旱，軍食不充，願且息役，以俟豐年。」

translations.literal: Chongtao remonstrated: "Now both river regions suffer drought; army provisions are insufficient—I ask that labor be suspended for now, to await a bountiful year."
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao remonstrated, "Both river regions suffer drought now; army provisions are insufficient—I ask that labor be suspended until a bountiful year."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 帝將伐蜀，辛卯，詔天下括市戰馬。

translations.literal: As the emperor prepared to attack Shu, on xinmao an edict ordered the realm to requisition war horses from the market.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to attack Shu, on xinmao an edict ordered the realm to requisition war horses from the market.

sentences.zh: 吳鎮海節度判官、楚州團練使陳彥謙有疾，徐知誥恐其遺言及繼嗣事，遺之醫藥金帛，相屬於道。

translations.literal: The Wu Zhenhai circuit judge-advisor and Chuzhou defense commissioner Chen Yanqian was ill; Xu Zhigao feared his dying words might touch the matter of succession and sent him physicians, medicines, gold, and silk in endless succession along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Zhenhai circuit judge-advisor and Chuzhou defense commissioner Chen Yanqian was ill; Xu Zhigao feared his dying words might touch the matter of succession and sent physicians, medicines, gold, and silk to him in an unbroken stream along the road.

sentences.zh: 彥謙臨終，密留中遺徐溫，請以所生子為嗣。

translations.literal: As Yanqian neared death, he secretly left a sealed testament for Xu Wen, asking that his newly born son be made heir.
translations.idiomatic: As Yanqian neared death, he secretly left a sealed testament for Xu Wen, asking that his newborn son be made heir.

sentences.zh: 太后疾甚。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's illness was grave.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲午，成德節度使李嗣源以邊事稍弭，表求入朝省太后，帝不許。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu, Chengde military governor Li Siyuan, finding border affairs somewhat eased, memorialized asking to enter court to visit the empress dowager; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu, Chengde military governor Li Siyuan, finding border affairs somewhat eased, memorialized asking to enter court to visit the empress dowager; the emperor would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，太后殂。

translations.literal: On renyin, the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 帝毀過甚，五日方食。

translations.literal: The emperor's grief exceeded measure; only after five days did he eat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's grief exceeded measure; only after five days did he eat.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸未，杖殺河南令羅貫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guiwei, the magistrate of Henan, Luo Guan, was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guiwei, the magistrate of Henan, Luo Guan, was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 初，貫為禮部員外郎，性強直，為郭崇韜所知，用為河南令。

translations.literal: Initially Luo Guan had been an assistant director in the Ministry of Rites; his nature was forceful and upright—Guo Chongtao noticed him and had him appointed magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Luo Guan had been an assistant director in the Ministry of Rites; forceful and upright by nature, he came to Guo Chongtao's notice and was appointed magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 為政不避權豪，伶宦請托，書積几案，一不報，皆以示崇韜，崇韜奏之，由是伶宦切齒。

translations.literal: In governing he did not shrink before the powerful; petitions from actors and eunuchs piled on his desk unanswered—all were shown to Chongtao, who reported them to the throne—wherefore actors and eunuchs gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: In governing he did not shrink before the powerful; petitions from actors and eunuchs piled on his desk unanswered—all were shown to Chongtao, who reported them to the throne—wherefore actors and eunuchs gnashed their teeth at him.

sentences.zh: 河南尹張全義亦以貫高伉，惡之，遣婢訴於皇后，後與伶宦共毀之，帝含怒未發。

translations.literal: Henan intendant Zhang Quanyi too found Luo Guan overbearing and hated him; he sent a maidservant to complain to the empress, who together with actors and eunuchs slandered Luo Guan—the emperor nursed anger but did not yet act.
translations.idiomatic: Henan intendant Zhang Quanyi too found Luo Guan overbearing and hated him; he sent a maidservant to complain to the empress, who together with actors and eunuchs slandered Luo Guan—the emperor nursed anger but did not yet act.

sentences.zh: 會帝自往壽安視坤陵役者，道路泥濘，橋多壞。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor went in person to Shou'an to inspect workers on the Kun Mausoleum—the roads were muddy and many bridges broken.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the emperor went in person to Shou'an to inspect workers on the Kun Mausoleum—the roads were muddy and many bridges broken.

sentences.zh: 帝問主者為誰，宦官對屬河南。

translations.literal: The emperor asked who was responsible; a eunuch replied it fell under Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked who was responsible; a eunuch replied it fell under Henan.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下貫獄；

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and imprisoned Luo Guan;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and imprisoned Luo Guan;

sentences.zh: 獄吏榜掠，體無完膚，明日，傳詔殺之。

translations.literal: the jailers tortured him until no patch of skin remained whole; the next day an order was transmitted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: the jailers tortured him until no patch of skin remained whole; the next day an order was transmitted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 崇韜諫曰：「貫坐橋道不修，法不至死。」

translations.literal: Chongtao remonstrated: "Luo Guan's offense of failing to maintain bridges and roads does not reach death by law."
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao remonstrated, "Luo Guan's offense of failing to maintain bridges and roads does not reach death by law."

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「太后靈駕將發，天子朝夕往來，橋道不修，卿言無罪，是黨也！」

translations.literal: The emperor raged: "The empress dowager's spirit carriage is about to depart—the Son of Heaven travels back and forth daily; bridges and roads unrepaired—and you say he is guiltless? You are shielding him!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, "The empress dowager's spirit carriage is about to depart—the Son of Heaven travels back and forth daily; bridges and roads unrepaired—and you say he is guiltless? You are shielding him!"

sentences.zh: 崇韜曰：「陛下以萬乘之尊，怒一縣令，使天下謂陛下用法不平，臣之罪也。」

translations.literal: Chongtao said, "Your Majesty, with the dignity of the supreme ruler, enraged at a county magistrate—if the realm says Your Majesty applies the law unfairly, the fault is mine."
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao said, "Your Majesty, with the dignity of the supreme ruler, enraged at a county magistrate—if the realm says Your Majesty applies the law unfairly, the fault is mine."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「既公所愛，任公裁之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Since he is one you favor, let you decide."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since he is one you favor, let you decide."

sentences.zh: 拂衣起入宮，崇韜隨之，論奏不已；

translations.literal: He swept his robes and rose into the palace; Chongtao followed, arguing and memorializing without cease;
translations.idiomatic: He swept his robes and rose into the palace; Chongtao followed, arguing and memorializing without cease;

sentences.zh: 帝自闔殿門，崇韜不得入。

translations.literal: the emperor himself shut the hall doors, and Chongtao could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor himself shut the hall doors, and Chongtao could not enter.

sentences.zh: 貫竟死，暴屍府門，遠近冤之。

translations.literal: Luo Guan died in the end; his corpse was displayed at the magistrate's gate, and far and near judged it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Guan died in the end; his corpse was displayed at the magistrate's gate, and far and near judged it an injustice.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，遣吏部侍郎李德休等賜吳越國王玉冊、金印，紅袍御衣。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Li Dexiu and others were dispatched to present the King of Wuyue with a jade register, golden seal, and red imperial robe.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Li Dexiu and others were dispatched to present the King of Wuyue with a jade register, golden seal, and red imperial robe.

sentences.zh: 九月，蜀主與太后、太妃游青城山，歷丈人觀、上清宮，遂至彭州陽平化、漢州三學山而還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Shu sovereign Wang Yan toured Mount Qingcheng with the empress dowager and Grand Consort, passing through Zhangren Abbey and Shangqing Palace, then reaching Pengzhou's Yangping transformation site and Hanzhou's Mount Sanxue before returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the Shu sovereign Wang Yan toured Mount Qingcheng with the empress dowager and Grand Consort, passing through Zhangren Abbey and Shangqing Palace, then reaching Pengzhou's Yangping transformation site and Hanzhou's Mount Sanxue before returning.

sentences.zh: 乙未，立皇子繼岌為魏王。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Prince Jiji was installed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Prince Jiji was installed as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，帝與宰相議伐蜀，威勝節度使李紹欽素諂事宣徽使李紹宏，紹宏薦「紹欽有蓋世奇才，雖孫、吳不如，可以大任。」

translations.literal: On dingyou, the emperor discussed attacking Shu with the chief ministers; Weisheng military governor Li Shaoqin had long flattered Palace Secretariat commissioner Li Shaohong, and Shaohong recommended, "Shaoqin has world-beating talent—even Sun Wu falls short; he can be greatly entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the emperor discussed attacking Shu with the chief ministers; Weisheng military governor Li Shaoqin had long flattered Palace Secretariat commissioner Li Shaohong, and Shaohong recommended, "Shaoqin has world-beating talent—even Sun Wu falls short; he can be greatly entrusted."

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜曰：「段凝亡國之將，奸諂絕倫，不可信也。」

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao said, "Duan Ning is a general of a fallen state, cunning and flattery beyond compare—not to be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao said, "Duan Ning is a general of a fallen state, cunning and flattery beyond compare—not to be trusted."

sentences.zh: 眾舉李嗣源，崇韜曰：「契丹方熾，總管不可離河朔。

translations.literal: The assembly proposed Li Siyuan; Chongtao said, "The Khitan blaze just now—the Overall Commander cannot leave the northern rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly proposed Li Siyuan; Chongtao said, "The Khitan blaze just now—the Overall Commander cannot leave the northern rivers.

sentences.zh: 魏王地當儲副，未立殊功，請依故事，以為伐蜀都統，成其威名。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei's station is that of heir apparent, yet he has won no outstanding merit—I ask by precedent that he be made overall commander for the Shu campaign, to establish his renown."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei's station is that of heir apparent, yet he has won no outstanding merit—I ask by precedent that he be made overall commander for the Shu campaign, to establish his renown."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「兒幼，豈能獨往，當求其副。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The boy is young—how could he go alone? I must find his deputy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The boy is young—how could he go alone? I must find his deputy."

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「無以易卿。」

translations.literal: Then he said, "There is none to replace you."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "There is none to replace you."

sentences.zh: 庚子，以魏王繼岌充西川四面行營都統，崇韜充東北面行營都招討制置等使，軍事悉以委之。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Prince of Wei Jiji was made overall commander of the four-sided Shu field headquarters; Chongtao was made northeastern overall pacification and disposition commissioner and the like—all military affairs were wholly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Prince of Wei Jiji was made overall commander of the four-sided Shu field headquarters; Chongtao was made northeastern overall pacification and disposition commissioner and the like—all military affairs were wholly entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 又以荊南節度使高季興充東南面行營都招討使，鳳翔節度使李繼曮充都供軍轉運應接等使，同州節度使李令德充行營副招討使，陝州節度使李紹琛充蕃漢馬步軍都排陳斬斫使兼馬步軍都指揮使，西京留守張筠充西川管內安撫應接使，華州節度使毛璋充左廂馬步都虞候，邠州節度使董璋充右廂馬步都虞候，客省使李嚴充西川管內招撫使，將兵六萬伐蜀，仍詔季興自取夔、忠、萬三州為巡屬。

translations.literal: Jingnan military governor Gao Jixing was also made southeastern overall pacification commissioner; Fengxiang military governor Li Jiyong was made overall army supply, transport, and liaison commissioner; Tongzhou military governor Li Lingde was made deputy field pacification commissioner; Shaanzhou military governor Li Shaochen was made overall array-and-charge commissioner for barbarian and Han cavalry and infantry and also overall cavalry and infantry commander; Western Capital garrison commander Zhang Jun was made Western Shu circuit pacification and liaison commissioner; Huazhou military governor Mao Zhang was made left-wing cavalry and infantry chief inspector; Binzhou military governor Dong Zhang was made right-wing cavalry and infantry chief inspector; guest-reception commissioner Li Yan was made Western Shu circuit recruitment commissioner; with sixty thousand troops they attacked Shu, and an edict further allowed Jixing to take for himself the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan as patrol dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan military governor Gao Jixing was also made southeastern overall pacification commissioner; Fengxiang military governor Li Jiyong was made overall army supply, transport, and liaison commissioner; Tongzhou military governor Li Lingde was made deputy field pacification commissioner; Shaanzhou military governor Li Shaochen was made overall array-and-charge commissioner for barbarian and Han cavalry and infantry and also overall cavalry and infantry commander; Western Capital garrison commander Zhang Jun was made Western Shu circuit pacification and liaison commissioner; Huazhou military governor Mao Zhang was made left-wing cavalry and infantry chief inspector; Binzhou military governor Dong Zhang was made right-wing cavalry and infantry chief inspector; guest-reception commissioner Li Yan was made Western Shu circuit recruitment commissioner; with sixty thousand troops they attacked Shu, and an edict further allowed Jixing to take for himself the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan as patrol dependencies.

sentences.zh: 都統置中軍，以供奉官李從襲充中軍馬步都指揮監押，高品李廷安、呂知柔充魏王府通謁。

translations.literal: The overall commander established a central army; tribute officer Li Congxi was made central army cavalry and infantry commander and superintendent; senior attendants Li Ting'an and Lü Zhirou were made palace liaison officers for the Prince of Wei's household.
translations.idiomatic: The overall commander established a central army; tribute officer Li Congxi was made central army cavalry and infantry commander and superintendent; senior attendants Li Ting'an and Lü Zhirou were made palace liaison officers for the Prince of Wei's household.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以工部尚書任圜、翰林學士李愚並參預都統軍機。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Minister of Works Ren Yuan and Hanlin academician Li Yu were both appointed to participate in the overall commander's military deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Minister of Works Ren Yuan and Hanlin academician Li Yu were both appointed to participate in the overall commander's military deliberations.

sentences.zh: 自六月甲午雨，罕見日星，江河百川皆溢，凡七十五日乃霽。

translations.literal: From the sixth month, jiawu day, it rained; sun and stars were rarely seen; rivers and all streams overflowed—in all seventy-five days before the skies cleared.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth month, jiawu day, it rained; sun and stars were rarely seen; rivers and all streams overflowed—in all seventy-five days before the skies cleared.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜以北都留守孟知祥有薦引舊恩，將行，言於上曰：「孟知祥信厚有謀，若得西川而求帥，無逾此人者。」

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao, because Northern Capital garrison commander Meng Zhixiang owed him old gratitude for recommendation, before departing told the emperor, "Meng Zhixiang is trustworthy, generous, and resourceful—if we take Western Shu and seek a military governor, none surpasses this man."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao, because Northern Capital garrison commander Meng Zhixiang owed him old gratitude for recommendation, before departing told the emperor, "Meng Zhixiang is trustworthy, generous, and resourceful—if we take Western Shu and seek a military governor, none surpasses this man."

sentences.zh: 又薦鄴都副留守張憲謹重有識，可為相，戊申，大軍西行。

translations.literal: He also recommended Ye Capital deputy garrison commander Zhang Xian, steady and discerning, as fit for chief minister; on wushen the great army marched west.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Ye Capital deputy garrison commander Zhang Xian, steady and discerning, as fit for chief minister; on wushen the great army marched west.

sentences.zh: 蜀安重霸勸王承休請蜀主東遊秦州。

translations.literal: Shu's An Chongba urged Wang Chengxiu to invite the Shu sovereign Wang Yan to tour Qinzhou in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's An Chongba urged Wang Chengxiu to invite the Shu sovereign Wang Yan to tour Qinzhou in the east.

sentences.zh: 承休到官，即毀府署，作行宮，大興力役，強取民間女子教歌舞，圖形遺韓昭，使言於蜀主；

translations.literal: When Chengxiu took up his post, he at once tore down the prefectural offices and built a traveling palace; he launched grand corvée labor, forcibly took common women to teach singing and dancing, sent their portraits to Han Zhao and had him speak to the Shu sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: When Chengxiu took up his post, he at once tore down the prefectural offices and built a traveling palace; he launched grand corvée labor, forcibly took common women to teach singing and dancing, sent their portraits to Han Zhao and had him speak to the Shu sovereign;

sentences.zh: 又獻花木圖，盛稱秦州山川土風之美。

translations.literal: he also presented a catalogue of flowers and trees, lavishly praising Qinzhou's mountains, rivers, and local customs.
translations.idiomatic: he also presented a catalogue of flowers and trees, lavishly praising Qinzhou's mountains, rivers, and local customs.

sentences.zh: 蜀主將如秦州，群臣諫者甚眾，皆不聽；

translations.literal: The Shu sovereign Wang Yan was about to go to Qinzhou; many ministers remonstrated, yet he heeded none;
translations.idiomatic: The Shu sovereign Wang Yan was about to go to Qinzhou; many ministers remonstrated, yet he heeded none;

sentences.zh: 王宗弼上表諫，蜀主投其表於地；

translations.literal: Wang Zongbi submitted a memorial of remonstrance; the Shu sovereign cast the memorial to the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongbi submitted a memorial of remonstrance; the Shu sovereign cast the memorial to the ground;

sentences.zh: 太后涕泣不食，止之，亦不能得。

translations.literal: the empress dowager wept and refused food to stop him, yet could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager wept and refused food to stop him, yet could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 前秦州節度判官蒲禹卿上表幾二千言，其略曰：「先帝艱難創業，欲傳之萬世。

translations.literal: Former Qinzhou judge-advisor Pu Yuqing submitted a memorial of nearly two thousand characters; in summary it read: "The late emperor labored through hardship to found the realm, wishing to pass it down for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qinzhou judge-advisor Pu Yuqing submitted a memorial of nearly two thousand characters; in summary it read, "The late emperor labored through hardship to found the realm, wishing to pass it down for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 陛下少長富貴，荒色惑酒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has known luxury from youth; you wander in licentiousness and delusion in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has known luxury from youth; you wander in licentiousness and delusion in wine.

sentences.zh: 秦州人雜羌、胡，地多瘴癘，萬眾困於奔馳，郡縣罷於供億。

translations.literal: Qinzhou's people mix with Di and Hu; the land is rife with miasma—myriad hosts are exhausted by forced marches, counties and prefectures broken by supply levies.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou's people mix with Di and Hu; the land is rife with miasma—myriad hosts are exhausted by forced marches, counties and prefectures broken by supply levies.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔久為仇讎，必生釁隙；

translations.literal: Fengxiang has long been our foe—clashes will surely arise;
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang has long been our foe—clashes will surely arise;

sentences.zh: 唐國方通歡好，恐懷疑貳。

translations.literal: Tang now seeks harmony and friendship—we risk arousing suspicion of divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Tang now seeks harmony and friendship—we risk arousing suspicion of divided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 先皇未嘗無故盤遊，陛下率意頻離宮闕。

translations.literal: The late emperor never wandered without cause; Your Majesty whimsically leaves the palace again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor never wandered without cause; Your Majesty whimsically leaves the palace again and again.

sentences.zh: 秦皇東狩，鑾駕不還；

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin toured east—his imperial carriage never returned;
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin toured east—his imperial carriage never returned;

sentences.zh: 煬帝南巡，龍舟不返。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang toured south—his dragon boat never returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang toured south—his dragon boat never returned.

sentences.zh: 蜀都強盛，雄視鄰邦，邊亭無烽火之虞，境內有腹心之疾，百姓失業，盜賊公行。

translations.literal: The Shu capital is strong, looking down on neighboring states; the frontier posts know no beacon-fire alarm—yet within the realm there is sickness at the heart: the people lose their livelihoods and bandits walk openly.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu capital is strong, looking down on neighboring states; the frontier posts know no beacon-fire alarm—yet within the realm there is sickness at the heart: the people lose their livelihoods and bandits walk openly.

sentences.zh: 昔李勢屈於桓溫，劉禪降於鄧艾，山河險固，不足憑恃。」

translations.literal: Of old Li Shi submitted to Huan Wen, Liu Shan surrendered to Deng Ai—steep rivers and mountains are not enough to rely upon.”
translations.idiomatic: Of old Li Shi submitted to Huan Wen, Liu Shan surrendered to Deng Ai—steep rivers and mountains are not enough to rely upon."

sentences.zh: 韓昭謂禹卿曰：「吾收汝表，俟主上西歸，當使獄吏字字問汝！」

translations.literal: Han Zhao said to Yuqing, “I have received your memorial; when the sovereign returns west, I shall have the prison clerks question you word by word!”
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhao said to Pu Yuqing, "I have received your memorial. When His Majesty returns from the west, I will have the jailers interrogate you on every word!"

sentences.zh: 王承休妻嚴氏美，蜀主私焉，故銳意欲行。

translations.literal: Wang Chengxiu's wife Lady Yan was beautiful; the Shu sovereign Wang Yan lusted after her privately—hence his keen desire to make the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengxiu's wife, Lady Yan, was beautiful, and the Shu sovereign Wang Yan coveted her in secret. That was why he was so eager to make the trip.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，排陳斬斫使李紹琛與李嚴將驍騎三千、步兵萬人為前鋒，招討判官陳乂至寶雞，稱疾乞留。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Marshaling and Execution Commissioner Li Shaochen and Li Yan led three thousand fierce horsemen and ten thousand infantry as the vanguard; expedition judge-advisor Chen Yi reached Baoji and claimed illness, begging to remain behind.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Marshaling and Execution Commissioner Li Shaochen and Li Yan led three thousand elite horsemen and ten thousand foot soldiers as the vanguard. Expedition judge-advisor Chen Yi reached Baoji, feigned illness, and asked to stay behind.

sentences.zh: 李愚厲聲曰：「陳乂見利則進，懼難則止。

translations.literal: Li Yu said in a harsh voice, “Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he fears hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu said sharply, "Chen Yi pushes forward when he sees advantage and pulls back when he fears danger.

sentences.zh: 今大軍涉險，人心易搖，宜斬以徇！」

translations.literal: Now the great army crosses perilous ground—hearts are easy to shake; he should be beheaded as an example!”
translations.idiomatic: The main army is now crossing treacherous terrain, and morale is easily unsettled. He should be executed to warn the rest!"

sentences.zh: 由是軍中無敢顧望者。

translations.literal: From this, within the army none dared hang back.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no one in the army dared hesitate or look back.

sentences.zh: 乂，薊州人也。

translations.literal: Yi was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi was from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，蜀主引兵數萬發成都，甲子，至漢州。

translations.literal: On guihai the Shu sovereign Wang Yan led several tens of thousands of troops from Chengdu; on jiazi he reached Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the Shu sovereign Wang Yan set out from Chengdu with tens of thousands of troops. On jiazi he reached Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 武興節度使王承捷告唐兵西上，蜀主以為群臣同謀沮己，猶不信，大言曰：「吾方欲耀武。」

translations.literal: Wuxing military governor Wang Chengjie reported that Tang troops were marching west; the Shu sovereign thought the ministers were in league to dissuade him, still did not believe it, and said loudly, “I am just about to display martial glory.”
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing military governor Wang Chengjie reported that Tang forces were advancing from the west. The Shu sovereign assumed his ministers were conspiring to hold him back and still refused to believe it. He proclaimed, "I am about to put our might on display."

sentences.zh: 遂東行。

translations.literal: He then traveled east.
translations.idiomatic: He continued east all the same.

sentences.zh: 在道與群臣賦詩，殊不為意。

translations.literal: On the road he composed poetry with his ministers, wholly unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way he composed verses with his ministers, entirely unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，李紹琛攻蜀威武城，蜀指揮使唐景思將兵出降；

translations.literal: On dingchou Li Shaochen attacked Shu's Weiwu Fort; Shu commander Tang Jingsi led his troops out to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Li Shaochen attacked Shu's Weiwu Fort. Shu commander Tang Jingsi marched out and surrendered;

sentences.zh: 城使周彥禋等知不能守，亦降。

translations.literal: fortress commander Zhou Yantian and others, knowing they could not hold it, also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fort commander Zhou Yantian and the others, seeing the fort could not be held, surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 景思，秦州人也。

translations.literal: Jingsi was a native of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jingsi was from Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 得城中糧二十萬斛。

translations.literal: They obtained two hundred thousand hu of grain within the city.
translations.idiomatic: They seized two hundred thousand hu of grain stored in the city.

sentences.zh: 紹琛縱其敗兵萬餘人逸去，因倍道趣鳳州，李嚴飛書以諭王承捷。

translations.literal: Shaochen released more than ten thousand defeated Shu troops to escape, then doubled his pace toward Fengzhou; Li Yan sent urgent letters to persuade Wang Chengjie.
translations.idiomatic: Shaochen let more than ten thousand defeated Shu soldiers go, then forced a march toward Fengzhou while Li Yan sent urgent messages urging Wang Chengjie to surrender.

sentences.zh: 李繼曮竭鳳翔蓄積以饋軍，不能充，人情憂恐。

translations.literal: Li Jiyong exhausted Fengxiang's stores to supply the army, yet could not fill the need; men grew anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiyong drained Fengxiang's reserves trying to feed the army but still could not meet demand, and morale turned anxious and fearful.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜入散關，指其山曰：「吾輩進無成功，不復得還此矣。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao entered San Pass, pointed at the mountain and said, “If we advance without success, we shall not return here again.
translations.idiomatic: Entering San Pass, Guo Chongtao pointed at the mountains and said, "If we press on and fail, we will never see this place again.

sentences.zh: 當盡力一決。

translations.literal: We must exert all our strength in one decisive effort.
translations.idiomatic: We must stake everything on one decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 今饋運將竭，宜先取鳳州，因其糧。」

translations.literal: Now supplies are nearly exhausted—we should first take Fengzhou and seize its grain.”
translations.idiomatic: Our supply lines are nearly spent. We should take Fengzhou first and live off its stores."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆言蜀地險固，未可長驅，宜按兵觀釁。

translations.literal: All the generals said Shu territory was perilous and firm; one could not drive deep—better to hold the army and watch for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued that Shu terrain was treacherous and strongly defended, that a long advance was reckless, and that they should hold their position and wait for an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 崇韜以問李愚，愚曰：「蜀人苦其主荒淫，莫為之用。

translations.literal: Chongtao asked Li Yu; Yu said, “The Shu people suffer under their ruler's wantonness and debauchery and will not serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao consulted Li Yu, who said, "The people of Shu are weary of their ruler's dissipation and debauchery. None will fight for him.

sentences.zh: 宜乘其人情崩離，風驅霆擊，彼皆破膽，雖有險阻，誰與守之！

translations.literal: We should ride their hearts scattering and breaking apart—storm-wind and thunder-strike; all their courage will be shattered; though there are barriers, who will defend them!
translations.idiomatic: Strike while their loyalty is collapsing—sweep in like wind and thunder. Their courage will be broken. However steep the passes, who will stand to defend them?

sentences.zh: 兵勢不可緩也。」

translations.literal: The momentum of the army must not be slackened.”
translations.idiomatic: We cannot afford to let the army's momentum stall."

sentences.zh: 是日李紹琛告秉，崇韜喜，謂李愚曰：「公料敵如此，吾復何憂！」

translations.literal: That day Li Shaochen reported the victory; Chongtao rejoiced and said to Li Yu, “You judge the enemy thus—what have I left to fear!”
translations.idiomatic: That same day Li Shaochen reported victory. Chongtao was delighted and told Li Yu, "With you reading the enemy this clearly, what do I have to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 乃倍道而進。

translations.literal: They then doubled their pace and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed forward at forced march.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，王承捷以鳳、興、文、扶四州印節迎降，得兵八千，糧四十萬斛。

translations.literal: On wuyin Wang Chengjie came to surrender bearing the seals and insignia of Feng, Xing, Wen, and Fu prefectures; they gained eight thousand troops and four hundred thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wang Chengjie surrendered with the official seals and regalia of Feng, Xing, Wen, and Fu prefectures, yielding eight thousand troops and four hundred thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 崇韜曰：「平蜀必矣！」

translations.literal: Chongtao said, “The pacification of Shu is assured!”
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao declared, "Shu is as good as pacified!"

sentences.zh: 即以都統牒命承捷攝武興節度使。

translations.literal: He immediately issued an overall-commander's order appointing Chengjie acting Wuxing military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately issued an order from overall command naming Chengjie acting military governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 己卯，蜀主至利州，威武敗卒奔還，始信唐兵之來。

translations.literal: On jimao the Shu sovereign reached Lizhou; Weiwu Fort's defeated troops fled back—only then did he believe Tang troops had come.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Shu sovereign reached Lizhou. When the shattered survivors from Weiwu Fort came streaming back, he finally believed the Tang army had invaded.

sentences.zh: 王宗弼、宋光嗣言於蜀主曰：「東川、山南兵力尚完，陛下但以大軍扼利州，唐人安敢懸兵深入！」

translations.literal: Wang Zongbi and Song Guangsi said to the Shu sovereign, “Dongchuan and Shannan's forces remain intact; Your Majesty need only hold Lizhou with the main army—how would Tang troops dare advance deep with a dangling army!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongbi and Song Guangsi told the sovereign, "Dongchuan and Shannan still have intact forces. If Your Majesty stations the main army at Lizhou, the Tang will never dare push deep with a force cut off from its base."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: He complied.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以隨駕清道指揮使王宗勳、王宗儼、兼侍中王宗昱為三招討，將兵三萬逆戰。

translations.literal: On gengchen the imperial escort Qingdao commander Wang Zongxun, Wang Zongyan, and concurrent palace attendant Wang Zongyu were made the three expeditionary commanders, leading thirty thousand troops to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he appointed imperial escort Qingdao commander Wang Zongxun and Wang Zongyan, together with palace attendant Wang Zongyu, as the three expeditionary commanders and sent thirty thousand men to give battle.

sentences.zh: 從駕兵自綿、漢至深渡，千里相屬，皆怨憤，曰：「龍武軍糧賜倍於它軍，它軍安能禦敵！」

translations.literal: The escort army from Mian, Han, to Shendu stretched a thousand li in unbroken file—all were resentful and angry, saying, “The Dragon Martial Army's grain and rewards are double the other armies—how can the other armies resist the enemy!”
translations.idiomatic: The escort army stretched in an unbroken line for a thousand li from Mian and Han to Shendu. The men were full of bitter resentment: "The Dragon Martial Army gets twice the rations and pay we do—how are the rest of us supposed to face the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 李紹琛等過長舉，興州都指揮使程奉璉將所部兵五百來降，且請先治橋棧以俟唐軍，由是軍行無險阻之虞。

translations.literal: Li Shaochen and others passed Changju; Xingzhou chief commander Cheng Fenglian led five hundred men of his command to surrender and asked to repair bridges and plank roads first to await Tang troops—thus the army marched without fear of barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaochen's force passed Changju. Xingzhou commander Cheng Fenglian came over with five hundred men and offered to repair bridges and plank roads ahead of the Tang advance, so the army could march without fear of the terrain.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，興州刺史王承鑒棄城走，紹琛等克興州，郭崇韜以唐景思攝興州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinsi Xingzhou prefect Wang Chengjian abandoned the city and fled; Shaochen and others took Xingzhou; Guo Chongtao appointed Tang Jingsi acting Xingzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Xingzhou prefect Wang Chengjian abandoned the city and fled. Shaochen's force took Xingzhou, and Guo Chongtao made Tang Jingsi acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，成州刺史王承樸棄城走。

translations.literal: On yiyou Chengzhou prefect Wang Chengpu abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Chengzhou prefect Wang Chengpu fled his city.

sentences.zh: 李紹琛等與蜀三招討戰於三泉，蜀兵大敗，斬首五千級，餘眾潰走。

translations.literal: Li Shaochen and others fought Shu's three expeditionary commanders at Sanquan; Shu troops were utterly defeated—five thousand heads cut off, the rest routed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaochen's force met Shu's three expeditionary commanders at Sanquan and routed them, taking five thousand heads. The rest broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 又得糧十五萬斛於三泉，由是軍食優足。

translations.literal: They also obtained one hundred fifty thousand hu of grain at Sanquan—thus army provisions became ample.
translations.idiomatic: They also seized one hundred fifty thousand hu of grain at Sanquan, and from then on the army ate well.

sentences.zh: 戊子，葬貞簡太后於坤陵。

translations.literal: On wuzi Empress Dowager Zhenjian was buried at Kun Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Empress Dowager Zhenjian was interred at Kun Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 蜀主聞王宗勳等敗，自利州倍道西走，斷桔柏津浮梁；

translations.literal: The Shu sovereign heard that Wang Zongxun and the others were defeated; from Lizhou he doubled his pace west, severing the pontoon bridge at Jiebai Ford;
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wang Zongxun and his colleagues had been defeated, the Shu sovereign fled west from Lizhou at forced march and cut the pontoon bridge at Jiebai Ford.

sentences.zh: 使中書令、判六軍諸衛事王宗弼將大軍守利州，且令斬王宗勳等三招討。

translations.literal: he sent Secretariat Director and Six Armies and Guard Affairs overseer Wang Zongbi to lead the main army holding Lizhou, and ordered the execution of Wang Zongxun and the other two expeditionary commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Secretariat Director Wang Zongbi, who also oversaw the Six Armies and Guard offices, to hold Lizhou with the main force and to execute Wang Zongxun and the other two expeditionary commanders.

sentences.zh: 李紹琛晝夜兼行趣利州。

translations.literal: Li Shaochen marched day and night together toward Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaochen forced night-and-day marches toward Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀武德留後宋光葆遺郭崇韜書，「請唐兵不入境，當舉巡屬內附；

translations.literal: Shu Wude garrison deputy Song Guangbao sent Guo Chongtao a letter: “If Tang troops do not enter the territory, I shall bring all jurisdictions under my patrol to submit within;
translations.idiomatic: Shu's Wude garrison deputy Song Guangbao wrote to Guo Chongtao: "If Tang forces stay out of our territory, I will bring every district under my jurisdiction to submit.

sentences.zh: 苟不如約，則背城決戰以報本朝。」

translations.literal: if the agreement is not kept, then I shall fight with my back to the wall to repay my dynasty.”
translations.idiomatic: If you break that promise, I will fight to the death from the city walls in loyalty to my court."

sentences.zh: 崇韜復書撫納之。

translations.literal: Chongtao replied with a letter soothing and accepting him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao answered with a reassuring letter accepting the offer.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏王繼岌至興州，光葆以梓、綿、劍、龍、普五州，武定節度使王承肇以洋、蓬、壁三州，山南節度使兼侍中王宗威以梁、開、通、渠、麟五州，階州刺史王承岳以階州，皆降。

translations.literal: On jichou Prince of Wei's heir Li Jiji reached Xingzhou; Guangbao with Zi, Mian, Jian, Long, and Pu prefectures, Wuding military governor Wang Chengzhao with Yang, Peng, and Bi prefectures, Shannan military governor and concurrent palace attendant Wang Zongwei with Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin prefectures, and Jiezhou prefect Wang Chengyue with Jiezhou—all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the Prince of Wei's heir Li Jiji reached Xingzhou. Guangbao surrendered with Zi, Mian, Jian, Long, and Pu; Wuding military governor Wang Chengzhao with Yang, Peng, and Bi; Shannan military governor and palace attendant Wang Zongwei with Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin; and Jiezhou prefect Wang Chengyue with Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 承肇，宗侃之子也。

translations.literal: Chengzhao was the son of Zongkan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzhao was a son of Wang Zongkan.

sentences.zh: 自餘城鎮皆望風款附。

translations.literal: The remaining cities and garrison towns all submitted upon the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Every other city and garrison submitted at the first sign of Tang success.

sentences.zh: 天雄節度使王承休與副使安重霸謀掩擊唐軍，重霸曰：「擊之不勝，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Tianxiong military governor Wang Chengxiu and vice commissioner An Chongba plotted a surprise strike on Tang troops; Chongba said, “If we strike and do not win, the great cause is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiong military governor Wang Chengxiu and vice commissioner An Chongba planned a surprise attack on the Tang army. Chongba said, "If we strike and fail, everything is lost.

sentences.zh: 蜀中精兵十萬，天下險固，唐兵雖勇，安能直度劍門邪！

translations.literal: Shu has one hundred thousand elite troops; the realm's barriers are firm—though Tang troops are brave, how could they drive straight through Jianmen!
translations.idiomatic: Shu still has a hundred thousand crack troops, and the land's defenses are the steepest in the realm. However bold the Tang may be, how could they march straight through Jianmen Pass?

sentences.zh: 然公受國恩，聞難不可不赴，願與公俱西。」

translations.literal: Yet you receive the state's grace; hearing peril you cannot but go—I wish to go west together with you.”
translations.idiomatic: Still, you owe the state a debt of gratitude, and when danger calls you cannot stay away. I am willing to go west with you."

sentences.zh: 承休素親信之，以為然。

translations.literal: Chengxiu had long trusted him closely and thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu, who had long trusted him, agreed.

sentences.zh: 重霸請賂羌人買文、扶州路以歸；

translations.literal: Chongba asked to bribe the Di tribesmen to buy the Wen and Fu prefecture road for return;
translations.idiomatic: Chongba proposed bribing the Di tribesmen for a route back through Wen and Fu prefectures;

sentences.zh: 承休從之，使重霸將龍武軍及所募兵萬二千人以從。

translations.literal: Chengxiu complied and had Chongba lead the Dragon Martial Army and twelve thousand recruited troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu agreed and sent Chongba west with the Dragon Martial Army and twelve thousand levies.

sentences.zh: 將行，州人餞於城外。

translations.literal: About to depart, the people of the prefecture saw them off outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to leave, the townspeople saw them off outside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 承休上道，重霸拜於馬前曰：「國家竭力以得秦、隴，若從開府還朝，誰當守之！

translations.literal: Chengxiu took the road; Chongba bowed before his horse and said, “The state exhausted its strength to gain Qin and Long—if the Commissioner returns to court, who shall hold them!
translations.idiomatic: Once Chengxiu was on the road, Chongba bowed before his horse and said, "The state spent its strength to win Qin and Long. If Your Commissionership returns to court, who will hold them?

sentences.zh: 開府行矣，重霸請為公留守。」

translations.literal: Commissioner, go; Chongba asks to remain behind and hold the post for you.”
translations.idiomatic: Go on, Commissioner. Let Chongba stay behind and govern in your name."

sentences.zh: 承休業已上道，無如之何，遂與招討副使王宗汭自文、扶而南。

translations.literal: Chengxiu was already on the road and could do nothing—thus he and expedition deputy commissioner Wang Zongxuan went south from Wen and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu was already on the road and could not turn back. He and expedition deputy Wang Zongxuan continued south through Wen and Fu.

sentences.zh: 其地皆不毛，羌人抄之，且戰且行，士卒凍餒，比至茂州，餘眾二千而已。

translations.literal: The land was all barren; Di tribesmen harried them; they fought as they marched—troops froze and starved; by the time they reached Maozhou only two thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: The country was barren wasteland. Di raiders harried them every step of the way. Soldiers froze and starved as they fought and marched. By the time they reached Maozhou, barely two thousand were left.

sentences.zh: 重霸遂以秦、隴來降。

translations.literal: Chongba then brought Qin and Long to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chongba thereupon surrendered Qin and Long to Tang.

sentences.zh: 高季興常欲取三峽，畏蜀峽路招討使張武威名，不敢進。

translations.literal: Gao Jixing had long wished to take the Three Gorges, but feared the fame of Shu's Three Gorges Route Expeditionary Commissioner Zhang Wu and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixing had long wanted to seize the Three Gorges but feared Shu's Three Gorges Route commissioner Zhang Wu and never dared move.

sentences.zh: 至是，乘唐兵勢，使其子行軍司馬從誨權軍府事，自將水軍上峽取施州。

translations.literal: At this time, riding Tang military momentum, he had his son acting chief of staff Conghui administer military headquarters affairs and personally led the navy up the gorge to take Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Now, taking advantage of Tang momentum, he had his son and chief of staff Conghui run headquarters while he personally led the fleet upriver to seize Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 張武以鐵鎖斷江路，季興遣勇士乘舟斫之。

translations.literal: Zhang Wu blocked the river road with iron chains; Jixing sent brave men in boats to chop through them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wu blocked the Yangtze with iron chains. Jixing sent warriors in boats to cut them.

sentences.zh: 會風大起，舟絓於鎖，不能進退，矢石交下，壞其戰艦，季興輕舟遁去。

translations.literal: Just then a great wind rose; boats snagged on the chains and could neither advance nor retreat—arrows and stones rained down, destroying their warships; Jixing escaped in a light boat.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden gale rose. The boats fouled on the chains and could neither advance nor retreat while bolts and stones rained down and smashed the warships. Jixing fled in a light skiff.

sentences.zh: 既而聞北路陷敗，以夔、忠、萬三州遣使詣魏王降。

translations.literal: Soon after he heard the northern route had collapsed in defeat; with Qian, Zhong, and Wan prefectures he sent envoys to the Prince of Wei to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the northern front had collapsed, he sent envoys offering Qian, Zhong, and Wan to the Prince of Wei in surrender.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜遺王宗弼等書，為陳利害；

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao sent Wang Zongbi and the others letters laying out gain and loss;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao wrote Wang Zongbi and the others laying out the stakes;

sentences.zh: 李紹琛未至利州，宗弼棄城引兵西歸。

translations.literal: before Li Shaochen reached Lizhou, Zongbi abandoned the city and led troops west in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Before Li Shaochen even reached Lizhou, Zongbi abandoned the city and marched west.

sentences.zh: 王宗勳等三招討追及宗弼於白芀，宗弼懷中探詔書示之曰：「宋光嗣令我殺爾曹。」

translations.literal: Wang Zongxun and the three expeditionary commanders caught up with Zongbi at Baicao; Zongbi drew an edict from his breast and showed it, saying, “Song Guangsi ordered me to kill you all.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongxun and the other expeditionary commanders caught up with Zongbi at Baicao Ford. Zongbi pulled an edict from his robe and showed them: "Song Guangsi ordered me to execute you."

sentences.zh: 因相持而泣，遂合謀送款於唐。

translations.literal: They then embraced and wept, and together plotted to offer submission to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: They embraced and wept together, then conspired to surrender to Tang.
